142202.text: Fixed DRA consumable capacity requests failing when the request used a fully-qualified capacity name. Requests work with both the unqualified name, as published by drivers (typically without the driver name prefix), and the fully-qualified name. A related, less likely problem also occurred when a DRA driver changed how it published capacity after some capacity had already been allocated.
142202.markdown: Fixed DRA consumable capacity requests failing when the request used a fully-qualified capacity name. Requests work with both the unqualified name, as published by drivers (typically without the driver name prefix), and the fully-qualified name. A related, less likely problem also occurred when a DRA driver changed how it published capacity after some capacity had already been allocated. ([#142202](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/142202), [@pohly](https://github.com/pohly)) [SIG API Machinery, Apps, Node and Scheduling]
142202.author: pohly
142202.pr_body:
#### What type of PR is this?

/kind bug

#### What this PR does / why we need it:

When the ResourceClaim requested "driver.example.com/bandwidth" and that DRA driver published the capacity as "bandwidth", the request failed. Same for the inverse case.

A less likely problem existed when a DRA driver flipped between publishing with and without its own driver name as prefix: the allocation result stored literally what came from the driver at the time of allocation, which then wouldn't be considered after flipping to the other format.

Nothing prevents DRA drivers and users from publishing resp. requesting the same capacity with and without driver name prefix. Validation could prevent this for ResourceSlices (driver name is known) but doesn't. It's probably also not worth doing because DRA drivers are trusted and  can trivially avoid this; validation would just add overhead. https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/142218 makes sure that DRA driver behave well.

Lookup for constraints resolves this conflict via "fully-qualified wins". Consumable capacity and CEL resolution was random (last one in map iteration wins), now also prefers fully-qualified.

#### Which issue(s) this PR is related to:

Fixes: https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/issues/140650

#### Special notes for your reviewer:

The fix is to normalize names (drop redundant prefix) before comparing. To support downgrades, the allocation result is written with the simpler name without the driver name as prefix because that is what was written in practice before.

I have included making the consumable capacities and CEL capacities/attributes lookup deterministic in this PR. The one about CEL could also be a separate PR, but it seems related enough to not add that review overhead.

#### Does this PR introduce a user-facing change?
```release-note
DRA consumable capacity: requesting capacity had to be done with the capacity name exactly as published by drivers, i.e. typically without the driver name prefix. When requesting with a fully-qualified name, the request failed. Now both unqualified and fully-qualified names work. A related, less likely problem existed when a DRA driver changed how it published capacity and some capacity was allocated already.
```

#### AI usage disclosure:

YES: test cases were written manually, then AI was used to fix the code based on a description what the solution should look like.

142214.text: Fixed `kubectl describe service` printing `+ 0 more...` after the endpoint list when exactly three ready endpoints were followed by not-ready endpoints.
142214.markdown: Fixed `kubectl describe service` printing `+ 0 more...` after the endpoint list when exactly three ready endpoints were followed by not-ready endpoints. ([#142214](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/142214), [@reckless-sherixx](https://github.com/reckless-sherixx))
142214.author: reckless-sherixx
142214.pr_body:
#### What type of PR is this?

/kind bug

#### What this PR does / why we need it:

`formatEndpointSlices` decided that the endpoint list was truncated as soon as it visited a fourth endpoint, but it made that decision before applying the readiness filter while only counting ready endpoints. With exactly three ready endpoints followed by a not-ready one, the not-ready endpoint set the flag without being counted and `kubectl describe service` printed:

```
Endpoints:  10.0.0.1:80,10.0.0.2:80,10.0.0.3:80 + 0 more...
```

This derives the `+ N more...` suffix from the number of ready endpoints after filtering, so the count and the truncation decision always agree. Both the ported and the headless (no ports) branch are fixed.

`TestFormatEndpointSlices` is new; its "three ready endpoints followed by a not ready endpoint" and headless cases fail before the change and pass after it. Also verified failing against the `v1.37.0` tag.

#### Which issue(s) this PR is related to:

Fixes #142209

#### Special notes for your reviewer:

The readiness filter was added in #126932; the `len(list) == max` check predates it and was correct as long as every visited endpoint was counted.

#### Does this PR introduce a user-facing change?

```release-note
Fixed kubectl describe service printing "+ 0 more..." after the endpoint list when exactly three ready endpoints are followed by not-ready endpoints.
```

142215.text: Fixed `kubectl describe node` printing `-9223372036854775808%` for per-Pod resource percentages on nodes that had not reported allocatable resources. The totals in the `Allocated resources` section use the same resource accounting as the per-Pod rows.
142215.markdown: Fixed `kubectl describe node` printing `-9223372036854775808%` for per-Pod resource percentages on nodes that had not reported allocatable resources. The totals in the `Allocated resources` section use the same resource accounting as the per-Pod rows. ([#142215](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/142215), [@reckless-sherixx](https://github.com/reckless-sherixx))
142215.author: reckless-sherixx
142215.pr_body:
#### What type of PR is this?

/kind bug

#### What this PR does / why we need it:

Two fixes to the per-pod rows of the "Non-terminated Pods" table in `kubectl describe node`:

1. The per-pod percentages divided by the node's allocatable CPU/memory with no zero guard. On a node without `status.allocatable` / `status.capacity` every row printed `100m (-9223372036854775808%)`. The "Allocated resources" totals right below already guard the same division and print `0%`; the rows now do the same via a small `percentOf` helper.

2. Since 97f00d18eeb the rows are computed with `UseStatusResources: true`, but `getPodsTotalRequestsAndLimits` still used the pod spec only, so during an in-place resize a row could show `500m (50%)` while the totals showed `100m (10%)` for the same pod. The totals now use the same `PodResourcesOptions` as the rows.

Two new tests, `TestDescribeNodeResourceWithoutAllocatable` and `TestDescribeNodeResourceUsesStatusResourcesForTotals`, fail before the change and pass after it. Also verified failing against the `v1.37.0` tag.

#### Which issue(s) this PR is related to:

Fixes #142210

#### Special notes for your reviewer:

Using status resources for the totals follows the scheduler, which accounts allocated (status) resources when they are present. If reviewers would rather have both rows and totals use the spec only, the one-line option change in `getPodsTotalRequestsAndLimits` can be replaced by dropping `UseStatusResources` from the rows instead; the important part is that both agree.

#### Does this PR introduce a user-facing change?

```release-note
kubectl describe node: per-pod resource percentages no longer print -9223372036854775808% on nodes that have not reported allocatable resources, and the "Allocated resources" totals now use the same resource accounting as the per-pod rows.
```


142216.text: Added support for selector strings using `!=` (for example `app!=web`) in commands that convert a selector into a LabelSelector, such as `kubectl create pdb --selector` and `kubectl set selector`; they are translated to a `NotIn` match expression.
142216.markdown: Added support for selector strings using `!=` (for example `app!=web`) in commands that convert a selector into a LabelSelector, such as `kubectl create pdb --selector` and `kubectl set selector`; they are translated to a `NotIn` match expression. ([#142216](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/142216), [@reckless-sherixx](https://github.com/reckless-sherixx))
142216.author: reckless-sherixx
142216.pr_body:
#### What type of PR is this?

/kind bug

#### What this PR does / why we need it:

`labels.Parse` accepts `key!=value`, but `metav1.ParseToLabelSelector`, which is documented as being kept in sync with that parser, had no case for `selection.NotEquals` and fell through to `"!=" is not a valid label selector operator`. As a result `kubectl create pdb --selector='app!=web'` and `kubectl set selector ... 'app!=web'` rejected a selector that works with `kubectl get -l`.

`key!=value` selects exactly what `key notin (value)` selects (both match when the key is absent), so this maps `NotEquals` to `LabelSelectorOpNotIn` with a single value.

`TestParseToLabelSelector` is new: it covers every operator, and for each parsed `LabelSelector` it also checks that `LabelSelectorAsSelector` matches the same label sets as `labels.Parse` of the original string. The `foo!=bar` case fails before the change and passes after it; also verified failing against the `v1.37.0` tag.

#### Which issue(s) this PR is related to:

Fixes #142211

#### Special notes for your reviewer:

`>` and `<` remain rejected with their existing explicit error; only `!=` changes.

#### Does this PR introduce a user-facing change?

```release-note
Selector strings using "!=" (for example `app!=web`) are now accepted by commands that convert a selector into a LabelSelector, such as `kubectl create pdb --selector` and `kubectl set selector`; they are translated to a `NotIn` match expression.
```

142247.text: Fixed an issue where a Job recreated with the same name as a recently deleted Job could remain unreconciled because it inherited pending Pod expectations from the previous Job.
142247.markdown: Fixed an issue where a Job recreated with the same name as a recently deleted Job could remain unreconciled because it inherited pending Pod expectations from the previous Job. ([#142247](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/142247), [@6democratickim9](https://github.com/6democratickim9)) [SIG Apps and Testing]
142247.author: 6democratickim9
142247.pr_body:
#### What type of PR is this?

/kind bug

#### What this PR does / why we need it:

The Job controller tracks pending Pod creations and deletions by namespace/name. If a Job is deleted while a Pod creation is in flight and another Job is immediately created with the same name, the replacement can inherit the old Job's unsatisfied expectation. `syncJob` then skips `manageJob`, leaving the replacement unreconciled until another event or the expectations timeout.

This change clears Pod expectations from the Job delete-event handler, matching the existing behavior of the ReplicaSet and DaemonSet controllers.

It also adds a deterministic integration test. The test blocks the old Job's Pod POST after the creation expectation has been raised, deletes and recreates the Job under the same name with a new UID, waits for the informer to observe the replacement, and then releases the old request. It verifies that the replacement Job is reconciled and receives its suspended condition.

Without the fix, the test reproduces the stale-UID status error from the issue and times out waiting for the replacement Job:

```
Precondition failed: UID in precondition: <old UID>, UID in object meta: <new UID>
```

With the fix, the integration test passes.

I was assigned to #142142 on September 16 and started investigating the reproduction and integration coverage before #142236 was opened. #142236 implements the same expectation cleanup with unit coverage; this PR includes the integration reproduction requested in the issue discussion.

#### Which issue(s) this PR is related to:

Fixes #142142

#### Special notes for your reviewer:

Local verification:

- The new integration test fails on unmodified `master` with the stale-UID error and an unreconciled replacement Job.
- The new integration test passes three consecutive runs with this change.
- `go test ./pkg/controller/job/...` passes.

#### Does this PR introduce a user-facing change?

```release-note
Fixed an issue where a Job recreated with the same name as a recently deleted Job could remain unreconciled because it inherited pending Pod expectations from the previous Job.
```

#### Additional documentation e.g., KEPs (Kubernetes Enhancement Proposals), usage docs, etc.:

```docs
NONE
```

#### AI usage disclosure:

AI assistance was used while investigating the controller flow and developing the integration test. I reviewed the changes and locally verified both the baseline failure and the fixed behavior using a real kube-apiserver and etcd.

142277.text: Changed `resource.Quantity` so that calling `String` or encoding a quantity no longer mutates the instance, which it previously did in some cases. If an instance needs its string representation multiple times, call `CacheString` to pre-populate the value while the caller owns the instance and can safely mutate it. This is only needed for instances not created by `ParseQuantity`, such as those built directly or modified through math operations.
142277.markdown: Changed `resource.Quantity` so that calling `String` or encoding a quantity no longer mutates the instance, which it previously did in some cases. If an instance needs its string representation multiple times, call `CacheString` to pre-populate the value while the caller owns the instance and can safely mutate it. This is only needed for instances not created by `ParseQuantity`, such as those built directly or modified through math operations. ([#142277](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/142277), [@pohly](https://github.com/pohly))
142277.author: pohly
142277.pr_body:
#### What type of PR is this?

/kind feature
/kind failing-test
/kind flake

#### What this PR does / why we need it:

Most of the time, String for a resource.Quantity as returned by ParseQuantity is safe to use concurrently, but not always: when the input string isn't already in the canonical form, then the instance has no cached string and String mutates it when first called, leading to data races. This also happens when encoding as protobuf because Size (another conceptually read-only method) mutates the instance when calling String. Encoding as JSON or CBOR don't do this.

Because it is not predictable for callers when String or encoding are safe when done concurrently, it is better to make both read-only, which matches the normal expectation.

#### Which issue(s) this PR is related to:

Fixes: https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/issues/141404

#### Special notes for your reviewer:

To mitigate potential performance regressions during decode + encode, ParseQuantity now always caches a string on all return paths. OTOH, this itself can cause a performance regression when the generated cached string isn't used. The expectation is that non-canonical input is the exception, so hopefully this won't matter.

/assign @jpbetz 

Loosely related to making Quantity safer to use (https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/issues/141166).

Brought up before in https://kubernetes.slack.com/archives/C0EG7JC6T/p1784208713996489, with no responses. As discussed there and in the issue, data races caused by this have been observed in the kubelet and kube-apiserver.

Mutation was added originally in:
https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/1ef19062096c4fcf8ddeaf3a46731d9f262a0c04/pkg/api/resource/quantity.go#L560-L563

Then converted to string in:
https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/26033

142292.text: Fixed a bug where duplicate (status, reason) volume health conditions, or more than 16 conditions, reported by a CSI driver caused kubelet pod status patching to fail with a 422 validation error, blocking pod deletion. kubelet now keeps only the first condition for each (status, reason) pair, up to 16 conditions.
142292.markdown: Fixed a bug where duplicate (status, reason) volume health conditions, or more than 16 conditions, reported by a CSI driver caused kubelet pod status patching to fail with a 422 validation error, blocking pod deletion. kubelet now keeps only the first condition for each (status, reason) pair, up to 16 conditions. ([#142292](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/142292), [@Pcmhacker-piro](https://github.com/Pcmhacker-piro)) [SIG Node and Storage]
142292.author: Pcmhacker-piro
142292.pr_body:
#### What type of PR is this?

/kind bug
/sig node
/sig storage

#### What this PR does / why we need it:

In `v1.PodVolumeHealth`, the `healthConditions` list is defined as:
```go
// +listType=map
// +listMapKey=status
// +listMapKey=reason
// +k8s:maxItems=16
```
Declarative validation in `pkg/apis/core/v1/zz_generated.validations.go` requires each condition to have a unique `(status, reason)` pair and caps the total items at 16.

When a CSI driver reports volume health statuses containing duplicate `(status, reason)` entries or more than 16 conditions:
1. `mapVolumeHealthConditions` in `pkg/volume/csi/csi_client.go` did not deduplicate or cap the entries.
2. When `syncPod` attempts to patch the pod status on the API server, the patch fails with validation error `422 Unprocessable Entity` (`duplicate value: {"status": ..., "reason": ...}`).
3. Because the status patch fails with an error, `syncPod` aborts before evaluating `m.canBeDeleted(pod, status)`, causing the pod to be stuck in terminating/deleting state and Kubelet to enter an infinite patch retry loop.

This PR fixes this issue by:
1. Deduplicating conditions by composite key `(Status, Reason)` (preserving the first occurrence) and capping at `maxVolumeHealthConditions = 16` in CSI client mapping (`mapVolumeHealthConditions`), where volume health conditions from CSI drivers are initially populated.
2. Normalizing `LastTransitionTime` in Kubelet `normalizeStatus` behind the `CSIVolumeHealth` feature gate.
3. Adding comprehensive unit tests in `pkg/volume/csi` and `pkg/kubelet/status`.

#### Which issue(s) this PR is related to:

Fixes #142280

```release-note
Fixed a bug where duplicate (status, reason) volume health conditions reported by a CSI driver caused Kubelet pod status patching to fail with a 422 validation error, blocking pod deletion.
```

142350.text: Added a `KeyGenerator` option to `SelfSignedCertKeyOptions` in `k8s.io/client-go/util/cert`, so self-signed certificates can be generated with a key algorithm other than RSA. The default remains a 2048-bit RSA key.
142350.markdown: Added a `KeyGenerator` option to `SelfSignedCertKeyOptions` in `k8s.io/client-go/util/cert`, so self-signed certificates can be generated with a key algorithm other than RSA. The default remains a 2048-bit RSA key. ([#142350](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/142350), [@antcybersec](https://github.com/antcybersec)) [SIG API Machinery and Auth]
142350.author: antcybersec
142350.pr_body:
#### What type of PR is this?

/kind feature

#### What this PR does / why we need it:

`GenerateSelfSignedCertKeyWithOptions` hardcoded `rsa.GenerateKey(cryptorand.Reader, 2048)` for both the CA and the serving certificate, so the apiserver's `--cert-dir` certificates (`server/options/serving.go`) and the loopback client certificate (`serving_with_loopback.go`) could not use a post-quantum key even once the rest of the stack could.

This adds a `KeyGenerator` option to `SelfSignedCertKeyOptions`. It defaults to the existing 2048-bit RSA key, so output is unchanged for every current caller.

Two behaviors follow from the key type rather than from configuration:

* `keyEncipherment` is asserted only for RSA keys. ML-DSA and ECDSA sign only, and asserting the usage for them produces a certificate no library will honor. This implements the note left in `GenerateSelfSignedCertKeyWithOptions` by #142273.
* A non-RSA key is encoded as PKCS#8; RSA keeps its PKCS#1 encoding so the default output is byte-for-byte what it was.

#### Which issue(s) this PR is related to:

Part of #141838

#### Special notes for your reviewer:

Tests cover RSA, ECDSA P-256, and ML-DSA-65. Each generates, parses back through `keyutil.ParsePrivateKeyPEM`, carries the expected key usages, and the serving certificate verifies against the generated CA, so the ML-DSA path is exercised end-to-end.

Rebased on #142273, which has merged. The note it left in GenerateSelfSignedCertKeyWithOptions about key encipherment is removed here, since the key type is now configurable and the usage follows the key.

/assign @everettraven
/sig api-machinery
/sig auth

#### Does this PR introduce a user-facing change?

```release-note
`SelfSignedCertKeyOptions` in `k8s.io/client-go/util/cert` accepts a `KeyGenerator`, allowing self-signed certificates to be generated with a key algorithm other than RSA. The default remains a 2048-bit RSA key.
```

YES. Claude Code was used to navigate the existing key algorithm handling, draft this change and its tests, and run the verification described above. I reviewed every line and am responsible for the result.

142395.text: Fixed a regression that never shipped in any release.
142395.markdown: Fixed a regression that never shipped in any release. ([#142395](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/142395), [@antcybersec](https://github.com/antcybersec))
142395.author: antcybersec
142395.pr_body:
#### What type of PR is this?

/kind bug

#### What this PR does / why we need it:

#141203 started rejecting a decimal exponent that does not fit the int32 scale. A <=1.37 apiserver accepted those spellings, narrowed the exponent to an int32 and stored the object with the text it was given, so master cannot read them back: `ParseQuantity` fails, and per #141166 the etcd3 store fails an entire LIST on the first object it cannot decode.

Following the recipe in https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/issues/141166#issuecomment-5817729514:

**What v1.37.1 actually does**, measured against the release branch:

| input | v1.37.1 |
| --- | --- |
| `1e4294967296` | parses, `AsInt64` = `(1, true)`, `String()` = `1e4294967296` |
| `1e4294967297` | parses, `AsInt64` = `(10, true)`, `String()` = `10` |
| `-1e4294967296` | parses, `AsInt64` = `(-1, true)` |
| `1e-4294967296` | parses, `AsInt64` = `(1, true)` |
| `1e8589934592` | parses, `AsInt64` = `(1, true)` |
| `1e9223372036854775807` | parses, narrows to `-1`, `String()` = `100e-3` |
| `1e9223372036854775808` | parse error, on 1.37 and on master |
| `1e2147483648`, `1e-2147483648` | parse, then hang while canonicalizing |

So the stored contract is narrowing, not clamping: `1e4294967296` means **1**. Clamping the exponent to `MaxInt32` would decode those objects as astronomically large values instead of the values they hold.

**The tests** in `quantity_compat_test.go` pin the decode path, the re-encode path and the protobuf round trip for the four spellings that 1.37 both accepted and could write. They pass unchanged on `release-1.37` (v1.37.1) and fail on master with `unable to parse quantity's suffix`, which is the regression.

**The fix** narrows the exponent the way 1.37 did. A scale of `math.MinInt32` stays rejected: negating it overflows int32, and 1.37 hung while canonicalizing such a quantity rather than writing it, so no stored object can carry one. That also keeps those two spellings out of the compatibility set, since a test for them could not pass on 1.37.

`TestInterpretExponentInt32Bounds` and the parse error baseline move back to describing the narrowing.

#### Which issue(s) this PR is related to:

Part of #141166

#### Special notes for your reviewer:

Two things deliberately left out, both wanting your call:

- **Rejecting these on write.** With this change `cpu: 1e4294967296` is accepted again and silently means 1. Rejecting it at admission needs the parser to report that it narrowed, which is the strict entry point below rather than something validation can see today.
- **The opt-in strict mode.** Per your note about not shipping a variant that fixes 1 of N, I did not add one here. `1e2147483648` still hangs, and `Add`/`Sub`/`String` still wrap or blow up at extreme scales, so a "strict" `ParseQuantity` today would still hand callers a quantity that hangs later. Happy to add it in a follow-up once those land, or in this PR if you would rather have it now.

/assign @jpbetz
/sig api-machinery

#### Does this PR introduce a user-facing change?

```release-note
Fixed a regression in 1.38 where resource quantities written by a 1.37 or older apiserver with a decimal exponent outside the int32 range, such as `1e4294967296`, could not be decoded, which failed reads of the whole collection.
```

#### What this PR does / why we need it:

Bumps `google.golang.org/grpc` from v1.82.2 to v1.84.0 and removes the pin added in #142036.

v1.82.2 does not contain the fix for CVE-2026-84304 (HTTP/2 DATA frame heap exhaustion, GHSA-vp52-pcj8-j9qc). The fix, grpc/grpc-go#9331, shipped only in v1.83.1 and later, and there is no v1.82.x backport. The kubelet gRPC probe client dials servers that pod authors control, so the client side of this bug is reachable from any pod. v1.84.0 also carries the CVE-2026-84303 fix (xDS, which we do not vendor).

grpc v1.83.0+ requires `cloud.google.com/go/auth`, which adds four modules from the unwanted list to the module graph: `s2a-go`, `enterprise-certificate-proxy`, `gax-go/v2` and `google.golang.org/api`. This takes option 1 of #142005 and records them in `status.unwantedReferences` with grpc as the only referencer, next to the existing `protoc-gen-validate` and `vtprotobuf` entries. The upstream removal (grpc/grpc-go#9385) is approved but targets grpc 1.86.

The second commit takes what the pin was holding back: the etcd modules to v3.7.2 (they require grpc v1.83.2), `otelgrpc` to v0.71.0 and `otlptracegrpc` to v1.45.0. `otlptracegrpc` v1.46.0 is not taken because it requires `grpc-gateway/v2` v2.30.0, which stays pinned. MVS also moves otel core to v1.46.0, `proto/otlp` to v1.11.0, `golang.org/x/net` to v0.58.0 and `go-logr/logr` to v1.4.4. 142429.text: Fixed a data race in kube-scheduler where concurrent Reject and Preempt calls on a Pod waiting at the Permit extension point could both report success.
142429.markdown: Fixed a data race in kube-scheduler where concurrent Reject and Preempt calls on a Pod waiting at the Permit extension point could both report success. ([#142429](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/142429), [@kojah](https://github.com/kojah))
142429.author: kojah
142429.pr_body:
#### What type of PR is this?

/kind bug

#### What this PR does / why we need it:

`waitingPod.stopWithStatus` (`pkg/scheduler/framework/runtime/waiting_pods_map.go`) sets `w.done` while holding only the read side of `w.mu`. `Reject` and `Preempt` can run at the same time, from two permit plugins or from their `time.AfterFunc` timeouts, so both callers can see `done == false` and both return `true`. `Allow` already takes the write lock for the same field, and this PR makes `stopWithStatus` do the same. The timeout callbacks run on their own goroutines after `newWaitingPod` releases the lock, so taking the write lock can't deadlock.

The new `TestWaitingPodConcurrentStop` rejects and preempts one pod from eight goroutines at once and expects exactly one call to succeed:

```
go test -race ./pkg/scheduler/framework/runtime/ -run TestWaitingPodConcurrentStop
```

With the old read lock, the test fails with `DATA RACE` on the first run. With the fix, it passes. Tested on linux/amd64 (16 cores) with Go 1.27.0.

#### Which issue(s) this PR is related to:

N/A

#### Special notes for your reviewer:

I found this race with [gohawk](https://gohawk.dev/), a static analyzer I work on. Its [`lockorder`](https://gohawk.dev/analyzers/concurrency-and-synchronization/lockorder/) analyzer reported it through the `read-lock-write` check.

This PR was written in part with the assistance of Claude (impl + regression tests). I reviewed the change by hand and tested the reproduction myself.

```release-note
Fixed a potential data race condition in the preemption workflow within the scheduling cycle.
```

142434.text: Updated `kubelet` to honor `serverCertificateKeyAlgorithm` when generating its self-signed serving certificate. Previously, that certificate was always RSA-2048. Now it uses the configured algorithm, defaulting to ECDSA-P256.
142434.markdown: Updated `kubelet` to honor `serverCertificateKeyAlgorithm` when generating its self-signed serving certificate. Previously, that certificate was always RSA-2048. Now it uses the configured algorithm, defaulting to ECDSA-P256. ([#142434](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/142434), [@antcybersec](https://github.com/antcybersec)) [SIG Auth and Node]
142434.author: antcybersec
142434.pr_body:
#### What type of PR is this?

/kind feature

#### What this PR does / why we need it:

`InitializeTLS` generates a self-signed serving certificate when neither `serverTLSBootstrap` nor an explicit certificate is configured. That path called `GenerateSelfSignedCertKey`, which always produces a 2048-bit RSA key, and ignored `serverCertificateKeyAlgorithm` even though it has `KubeletConfiguration` in hand.

Nothing rejects the combination, so the field is silently dropped: config validation accepts `serverCertificateKeyAlgorithm` regardless of `serverTLSBootstrap`, and only requires TLS 1.3 for the ML-DSA variants. The bootstrapped path already honors the field (`pkg/kubelet/certificate/kubelet.go`), so the two ways a kubelet can get a serving certificate disagreed—and they disagreed even with the field unset, since it documents and defaults to ECDSA-P256 while this path produced RSA-2048.

This PR passes the same key generator the bootstrapped path uses, via the `GenerateKey` option added in #142350. A cluster asking for ML-DSA serving keys now gets them on both paths.

Part of #141838.

#### Which issue(s) this PR fixes:

Fixes #

#### Special notes for your reviewer:

New table test `TestInitializeTLSSelfSignedKeyAlgorithm` asserts the exact key in the generated certificate (curve for ECDSA, bit length for RSA, parameter set for ML-DSA) across unset / ECDSA-P384 / RSA-4096 / ML-DSA-65. Verified all four fail without the change—the unset case reports generated cert key = RSA 2048, want ECDSA P-256.

#### Does this PR introduce a user-facing change?

```release-note
Kubelet now honors serverCertificateKeyAlgorithm when generating its self-signed serving certificate. Previously that certificate was always RSA-2048; it now uses the configured algorithm, defaulting to ECDSA-P256 as documented.
```

142443.text: Fixed API warnings on ReplicationController updates, which described the previous pod template instead of the new one.
142443.markdown: Fixed API warnings on ReplicationController updates, which described the previous pod template instead of the new one. ([#142443](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/142443), [@thc1006](https://github.com/thc1006)) [SIG Apps]
142443.author: thc1006
142443.pr_body:
#### What type of PR is this?

/kind bug
/sig apps

#### What this PR does / why we need it:

`rcStrategy.WarningsOnUpdate` passes the templates in the wrong order:

```go
		warnings = pod.GetWarningsForPodTemplate(ctx, field.NewPath("spec", "template"), oldRc.Spec.Template, newRc.Spec.Template)
```

`GetWarningsForPodTemplate` takes `(ctx, fieldPath, podTemplate, oldPodTemplate)`, and the other workload strategies pass the new template first. So the warnings on a ReplicationController update describe the template it had before the update.

Before and after on a kind cluster. The `###` lines come from my script, which also prints commands without their shell quoting. Its exit-code lines and blank lines are removed and the file path is shortened, the rest is as printed:

```
### apiserver v1.38.0-alpha.0.1170+dfd7b93a178387
$ kubectl -n rctest apply -f rc.json
replicationcontroller/rc created
$ kubectl -n rctest patch replicationcontroller rc -p {"spec":{"template":{"spec":{"terminationGracePeriodSeconds":-1}}}}
replicationcontroller/rc patched
$ kubectl -n rctest patch replicationcontroller rc -p {"spec":{"template":{"spec":{"terminationGracePeriodSeconds":30}}}}
Warning: spec.template.spec.terminationGracePeriodSeconds: must be >= 0; negative values are invalid and will be treated as 1
replicationcontroller/rc patched
### apiserver v1.38.0-alpha.0.1171+00b5ea25a9b98d
$ kubectl -n rctest apply -f rc.json
replicationcontroller/rc created
$ kubectl -n rctest patch replicationcontroller rc -p {"spec":{"template":{"spec":{"terminationGracePeriodSeconds":-1}}}}
Warning: spec.template.spec.terminationGracePeriodSeconds: must be >= 0; negative values are invalid and will be treated as 1
replicationcontroller/rc patched
$ kubectl -n rctest patch replicationcontroller rc -p {"spec":{"template":{"spec":{"terminationGracePeriodSeconds":30}}}}
replicationcontroller/rc patched
```

The new test fails on the base commit in the two cases where the order matters. The swap goes back to #101688.

With both PRs on a kind cluster, changing an RC from 1 to 0 warns and changing it back does not; with #142444 alone it is the other way round. So this one should go in first.

142457.text: Changed the `kubelet` gRPC probes to fail immediately when the connection is refused, instead of retrying until the probe timeout. The failure message for a server that never answers changed to "timeout: health rpc did not complete within <timeout>".
142457.markdown: Changed the `kubelet` gRPC probes to fail immediately when the connection is refused, instead of retrying until the probe timeout. The failure message for a server that never answers changed to "timeout: health rpc did not complete within <timeout>". ([#142457](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/142457), [@dims](https://github.com/dims)) [SIG Node and Testing]
142457.author: dims
142457.pr_body:
#### What type of PR is this?

/kind cleanup

#### What this PR does / why we need it:

Moves the gRPC probe from the deprecated `grpc.DialContext` with `WithBlock` to `grpc.NewClient`. The client does no I/O until the health check runs, so the one probe timeout still covers connect and RPC. The target uses the `passthrough` resolver, which hands the address to the probe dialer unresolved, as `DialContext` did by default; `NewClient` would otherwise pick the `dns` resolver. Connection errors now surface from the RPC as `Unavailable` and map to the existing "failed to connect" message.

Behavior change: a refused connection fails the probe at once instead of retrying until `timeoutSeconds`, and a server that never answers reports `timeout: health rpc did not complete within <timeout>` instead of `timeout: failed to connect service`. Probe outcomes do not change.

The unreachable-host test, which asserted the old exact timeout text against port 32, is replaced by a connection-refused test on a closed local port that also checks the probe returns well before its 10s timeout. Precedent: #137955 did the same move for cri-client. The second commit fixes a pre-existing flake in two container lifecycle tests (`exit -1` in busybox) that failed this PR's node e2e run; the comment below has the history.

142458.pr_body:
#### What type of PR is this?

#### What this PR does / why we need it:

The pods API gRPC server rate-limits unary calls but not `WatchPods` streams, and grpc defaults to unlimited concurrent streams. Every client already holds node power through the root-only socket, so this is hygiene: a leaking monitoring agent could otherwise hold unlimited watch streams. The server now caps concurrent streams per connection at 100 and runs stream openings through the same rate limiter as unary calls, via a stream interceptor next to the existing unary one.

142509.markdown: Added the `PullSecurityProfile`, `ListSecurityProfiles`, and `RemoveSecurityProfile` RPCs, the `OCI` seccomp profile type with `oci_ref` and `SecurityProfileBase`, the `seccomp_profile_oci` runtime feature, and the `SecurityProfileInvalid` well-known error to the CRI API for seccomp profiles pulled from OCI registries (Alpha). 142509.pr_body:
#### What type of PR is this?

/kind feature
/kind api-change
/sig node

#### What this PR does / why we need it:

CRI API for KEP-6061: the `OCI` seccomp profile type (`oci_ref`, `base_profile`), the `ImageService` RPCs `PullSecurityProfile`, `ListSecurityProfiles`, and `RemoveSecurityProfile`, the `seccomp_profile_oci` runtime feature, and the `SecurityProfileInvalid` well-known error. The proto documents the lifecycle and error contract for runtimes. Client, fakes, instrumented service, and e2e CRI proxies implement the RPCs; the kubelet does not call them yet.

#### Which issue(s) this PR is related to:

KEP: https://github.com/kubernetes/enhancements/issues/6061

#### Special notes for your reviewer:

First PR of the chain, so CRI-O and containerd can build against it. `SecurityProfileKind` values are unprefixed as in the KEP (like `SupplementalGroupsPolicy`). `seccomp_profile_oci` is node-wide rather than per runtime handler, because the merge happens before the OCI spec reaches the handler. Differences from the KEP, reconciled in one KEP update once the implementation is done: the proto does not define the artifact format (which formats a runtime accepts and how it validates them is up to the runtime, with the KEP's format as the recommendation); `ListSecurityProfiles` and `RemoveSecurityProfile` move from beta to alpha, so the kubelet owns the lifecycle of pulled profiles from the start; `SecurityProfileBase.BaseType` has `RuntimeDefault` as its zero value instead of an unspecified value; the merge is two-way, the base profile (the runtime default unless the pod spec selects a `Localhost` base) intersected with the OCI profile, instead of the KEP's three-way merge with the runtime baseline as a floor; `oci_ref` or `base_profile` on another profile type is rejected as a kubelet programming error; and `SecurityProfileKind` has no reserved `AppArmor` value (beta adds one if it needs it).

#### Does this PR introduce a user-facing change?

```release-note
CRI API: added the `PullSecurityProfile`, `ListSecurityProfiles`, and `RemoveSecurityProfile` RPCs, the `OCI` seccomp profile type with `oci_ref` and `SecurityProfileBase`, the `seccomp_profile_oci` runtime feature, and the `SecurityProfileInvalid` well-known error, for seccomp profiles pulled from OCI registries (Alpha).
```

Privileged containers cannot use an `OCI` profile, and Pod Security admission rejects `OCI` profiles at the Baseline and Restricted levels. The kubelet in this release does not pull or apply OCI seccomp profiles. ([#142511](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/142511), [@saschagrunert](https://github.com/saschagrunert)) [SIG API Machinery, Apps, Autoscaling, CLI, Node, Scheduling and Testing]
142511.author: saschagrunert
142511.pr_body:
#### What type of PR is this?

/kind feature
/kind api-change
/sig node
/label api-review

#### What this PR does / why we need it:

API for KEP-6061: `seccompProfile.type: OCI` with `oci.ref` (digest-pinned, no tag) and an optional `oci.baseProfile` (`RuntimeDefault` or `Localhost`), behind the alpha `SecurityProfileOCI` gate. Privileged containers cannot use an `OCI` profile, set or inherited. With the gate off the type is rejected unless already in use; nothing is dropped. PodSecurity keeps rejecting `OCI` in alpha. Adds the `SecurityProfileOCI` node declared feature; kubelets declare it once #142515 feeds the runtime feature in. Skew: kubelets before v1.38 fell through to `Unconfined` on an unknown type, which the declared feature, PodSecurity and the v1.41 beta floor cover (see the KEP).

#### Which issue(s) this PR is related to:

KEP: https://github.com/kubernetes/enhancements/issues/6061

#### Special notes for your reviewer:

The `oci` field is validated declaratively (unions, enum, `maxLength` on `ref` and `baseProfile.localhostProfile`, `+k8s:customValidation` for the reference and the local path in `pkg/apis/core/v1`); the gate check and the privileged rule stay handwritten. The generator requires `+k8s:alpha(since: "1.38")=+k8s:optional` on the parents and migrates `seccompProfile.type` required as alpha. Static pods get only the handwritten validation, so #142515 checks the base profile path in the kubelet. Follow-ups: `kubectl describe` for the new fields, a non-OCI debug container profile for `kubectl debug --profile=sysadmin`.

Deltas from the KEP, to be folded in: `oci.ref` instead of `oci.reference` (kube-api-linter), `ref` capped at 1024 characters, declarative validation, no field stripping, the declared feature requires the `seccomp_profile_oci` runtime feature, and the two-way merge from #142509 (a `Localhost` base replaces the runtime default).

```release-note
Added (Alpha) support for OCI distribution of seccomp profiles. With the `SecurityProfileOCI` feature gate enabled, Kubernetes allows specifying seccomp profiles pulled from OCI registries, `seccompProfile.type: OCI` in a Pod spec, with a digest-pinned `oci.ref` and an optional `oci.baseProfile`.
```

142527.text: Fixed `k8s.io/apimachinery/pkg/util/yaml` silently dropping the last line of a YAML stream when it has no trailing newline and its length is an exact multiple of the reader buffer size.
142527.markdown: Fixed `k8s.io/apimachinery/pkg/util/yaml` silently dropping the last line of a YAML stream when it has no trailing newline and its length is an exact multiple of the reader buffer size. ([#142527](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/142527), [@SLoeuillet](https://github.com/SLoeuillet))
142527.author: SLoeuillet
142527.pr_body:
#### What type of PR is this?

/kind bug
/sig api-machinery

#### What this PR does / why we need it:

`YAMLReader` silently dropped the last line of a stream when that line had no trailing newline and a length that is an exact multiple of the buffer size. In that case `LineReader.Read` returns the line together with `io.EOF` (as `io.Reader` allows), and `YAMLReader.Read` discarded it. `YAMLReader.Read` now keeps a line returned with `io.EOF`, ignoring the bare `"\n"` that `LineReader` appends at a normal EOF; writing that one too would make `Read` never return `io.EOF`.

The added test fails at 4096, 8192 and 16384 bytes without the fix, and passes at 4095 and 4097 either way.

#### Which issue(s) this PR is related to:

Fixes #142526

#### Special notes for your reviewer:

Real-world trigger: Argo CD strips the trailing newline from plugin output before decoding it, so a Helm chart whose last line was 16384 bytes was applied truncated.

#### Does this PR introduce a user-facing change?

```release-note
Fixed k8s.io/apimachinery/pkg/util/yaml silently dropping the last line of a YAML stream when it has no trailing newline and its length is an exact multiple of the reader buffer size.
```

142534.author: ArangoGutierrez
142534.pr_body:
#### What type of PR is this?

/kind cleanup
/sig scheduling

#### What this PR does / why we need it:

`cache.NewSnapshot` builds its node lists by ranging over a map, so the same pods and nodes can
produce a different node order on each call. This lists nodes in the order of the `nodes` argument,
followed by the node names that only appear in `pods`. The entries themselves are unchanged.

Two tests sorted the list themselves to get a stable order (`default_preemption_test.go`,
`preemption_test.go`); the second commit removes that sorting. Out-of-tree simulators such as kubernetes-sigs/scheduler-library, which
build snapshots with this helper, get different results from identical inputs.

#### Which issue(s) this PR is related to:

Related to https://github.com/kubernetes-sigs/scheduler-library/issues/43, where
`SchedulingSimulator.NewClusterSnapshot` places the same pod on different nodes from identical
inputs because it builds its snapshot with `cache.NewSnapshot`. That issue lists this PR as the
upstream route, alongside a change in the library itself; the library would pick it up with a later
k8s.io/kubernetes bump.

#### Special notes for your reviewer:

#### Does this PR introduce a user-facing change?

```release-note
`NewSnapshot` in `k8s.io/kubernetes/pkg/scheduler/backend/cache` now lists nodes in a deterministic order: the order of its `nodes` argument, followed by node names that only appear in pods, in pod order. Previously the order could change between calls with the same input.
```

142574.text: Fixed a reference counting leak in the Node authorizer graph for Pods that reference Secrets, ConfigMaps, or PersistentVolumeClaims multiple times.
142574.markdown: Fixed a reference counting leak in the Node authorizer graph for Pods that reference Secrets, ConfigMaps, or PersistentVolumeClaims multiple times. ([#142574](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/142574), [@liggitt](https://github.com/liggitt))
142574.author: liggitt
142574.pr_body:
Multiple references from one object to another object can exist:

* pod → multiple references to the same secret / configmap / resourceclaim / pvc
* pv → multiple references to the same secret

When adding to the graph, avoid adding the same edge multiple times, since that also increments the destination index multiple times. When edges are removed, that index is only decremented a single time per edge.

Added covering unit tests.

/sig auth
/cc @enj

```release-note
Fixed refcounting leak in the node authorizer graph for pods which reference secrets, configmaps, or pvcs multiple times
```

142575.text: Improved memory and CPU efficiency when decoding JSON lists into `unstructured.UnstructuredList` (such as in the dynamic client and `kubectl get -o json`), reducing memory usage by approximately half and decode time by about one third.
142575.markdown: Improved memory and CPU efficiency when decoding JSON lists into `unstructured.UnstructuredList` (such as in the dynamic client and `kubectl get -o json`), reducing memory usage by approximately half and decode time by about one third. ([#142575](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/142575), [@QHarshil](https://github.com/QHarshil))
142575.author: QHarshil
142575.pr_body:
#### What type of PR is this?

/kind cleanup
/sig api-machinery

#### What this PR does / why we need it:

`decodeToList` read each list item three times: into `list.Object` with the items included, into a struct that collected the raw items, and again from each item's raw bytes. The dynamic client's `List` and `kubectl get -o json` go through it.

This PR decodes the list once with json/v2, following liggitt's suggestion in review. `util/json` gets `CaseSensitivePreserveIntsV2Options`, which decodes like `Unmarshal` into `interface{}` values. `decodeToList` decodes `items` as maps and every other member into `list.Object`.

`BenchmarkDecodeList`, 12 runs, go1.27.0, Apple M4 Pro. Time is the fastest run, as the machine was loaded.

| | master | this PR |
|---|---|---|
| pods-10 | 220µs, 226KiB, 4,243 allocs | 148µs, 117KiB, 2,657 allocs |
| pods-1000 | 22ms, 21.9MiB, 421k allocs | 15ms, 11.2MiB, 263k allocs |
| large-strings-10 | 9.7ms, 3.3MiB, 510 allocs | 0.8ms, 1.1MiB, 274 allocs |

Well-formed lists decode as before. I compared master and this branch locally over 22,000 inputs through every `UnstructuredJSONScheme` entry point, including list responses recorded from a kube-apiserver, and over dynamic client, informer and `kubectl get` output. Malformed input differs in error text, in what a failed decode leaves in the list, and in repeated `items` keys: master keeps the last array and this merges the arrays element by element. Decoding `null` into a list that already has content keeps its members.

json/v2 is slower than master for lists with large members other than `items` and for deeply nested arrays inside items, by up to 1.5x. It allocates several times as many objects for arrays of bare booleans or nulls, with half the bytes. List responses have small top-level members, while deep nesting and boolean arrays are possible in custom resources.

#### Which issue(s) this PR is related to:

N/A

#### Special notes for your reviewer:

```
make test WHAT=./staging/src/k8s.io/apimachinery/...
go test -run '^$' -bench BenchmarkDecodeList -count 12 ./staging/src/k8s.io/apimachinery/pkg/apis/meta/v1/unstructured/
```

`make test` also passes for client-go, cli-runtime, kubectl, apiextensions-apiserver, and the apiserver endpoints and admission packages.

#### Does this PR introduce a user-facing change?

```release-note
Decoding JSON lists into `unstructured.UnstructuredList`, as the dynamic client and `kubectl get -o json` do, now uses about half the memory, and decode time drops by about a third.
```

YES. An AI coding assistant (Claude Opus 5.5) helped write the change and the tests. I reviewed the diff, and ran the tests and benchmarks.

<!--

Optionally add one or more of the following kinds if applicable:
/kind api-change
/kind deprecation
/kind failing-test
/kind flake

-->

#### What this PR does / why we need it:

Part of KEP-3953 ([In-place Node Resource Resize](https://github.com/kubernetes/enhancements/tree/master/keps/sig-node/3953-in-place-node-resource-resize)), scheduler side.

When the scheduler nominates a pod to a node and starts preemption, the victims enter their termination grace period. If the node's allocatable shrinks during that window so that the pod can no longer fit on the node even when it is empty, the nomination is stale: the node can never host the pod.

Without a queueing hint, the nominated pod stays in the unschedulable queue until the victims finish terminating. Only then is it re-filtered against the updated allocatable, found unschedulable-and-unresolvable on that node, and sent to preempt elsewhere. The wait is bounded by the victims' grace period and is wasted.

This PR extends the NodeResourcesFit node-update queueing hint. It returns
Queue only when all of these hold:
- the updated node is the pod's NominatedNodeName,
- the pod fit that node before the update, and
- the pod no longer fits it after the update.

Note:  this covers pod-by-pod preemption only. PodGroups waiting for victims do not benefit, because PodGroupEvaluator has no UnschedulableAndUnresolvable escape path.

142607.text: Fixed `kube-apiserver` and other servers built on `k8s.io/apiserver` so they accept up to 16384 request header values. Without this, the Go `v1.27` default limit of 500 header values rejects impersonated or proxied users with about 500 or more groups with HTTP 431. Releases built with Go `v1.26` had no separate header-count limit.
142607.markdown: Fixed `kube-apiserver` and other servers built on `k8s.io/apiserver` so they accept up to 16384 request header values. Without this, the Go `v1.27` default limit of 500 header values rejects impersonated or proxied users with about 500 or more groups with HTTP 431. Releases built with Go `v1.26` had no separate header-count limit. ([#142607](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/142607), [@cwedgwood](https://github.com/cwedgwood)) [SIG API Machinery and Auth]
142607.author: cwedgwood
142607.pr_body:
#### What type of PR is this?

/kind bug
/kind regression
/sig api-machinery

#### What this PR does / why we need it:

Go 1.27 rejects requests with more than 500 header values by default (`http.Server.MaxHeaderValueCount`, golang/go#79936), independently of `MaxHeaderBytes`. Impersonation and request-header authentication carry one header line per group, so a kube-apiserver built with Go 1.27 returns 431 for users with about 500 groups before authentication runs. Details and a reproduction are in #142606.

This sets `MaxHeaderValueCount` to 16384 for secure serving and deprecated insecure serving: the existing 1 MiB `MaxHeaderBytes` at about 64 bytes per value (~16 for the header name and ~48 for the value). The limit stays bounded against floods of tiny headers while accepting identities with thousands of groups.

The new test (Go 1.27 only) serves through `SecureServingInfo` and checks that 1,000 and 16,334 repeated `Impersonate-Group` values reach the handler over HTTP/1.1 and HTTP/2, and that 16,385 are rejected with 431.

With kube-apiserver built from this branch, impersonation and request-header requests with up to 1,000 groups return 200 over both protocols. v1.38.0-alpha.1 returns 431 from 495 groups over HTTP/2 and from 500 over HTTP/1.1.

#### Which issue(s) this PR is related to:

Fixes #142606

#### Special notes for your reviewer:

- A constant keeps this change small. Alternatives: a `SecureServingInfo` field so embedders can choose, a flag (an operator knob with no current tuning guidance), or deriving it from `MaxHeaderBytes`.
- Aggregated API servers built on `k8s.io/apiserver` pick this up. Servers that construct their own `http.Server` need the same change.
- `MaxHeaderValueCount` is new in Go 1.27, so `setMaxHeaderValueCount` has a go1.27 build-tagged implementation and a no-op for older Go. This commit applies cleanly to release-1.34 through 1.37 and passes `go vet` there with Go 1.26.8; release-1.34 needs the year-bearing copyright header in the new files.

#### Does this PR introduce a user-facing change?

```release-note
kube-apiserver and other servers built on k8s.io/apiserver now accept up to 16384 request header values. Without this, Go 1.27's default of 500 rejects impersonated or proxied users with about 500 or more groups with HTTP 431. Releases built with Go 1.26 had no separate header-count limit.
```

#### AI usage disclosure:

YES. AI tools were used to reproduce the problem, draft the change and test, and draft this description. I reviewed the change and am responsible for it.

142623.text: Fixed a race condition in `kube-scheduler` async preemption where a preemptor pod could remain stuck in the unschedulable queue if its last victim pod was already deleted before the preemption API call executed. Changed the boolean return value of `preemption.Executor.PreemptPod` in `pkg/scheduler/framework/preemption` to return `true` when the API server deletes a bound victim (and will emit a pod deletion event), and `false` when the victim was preempted only in scheduler memory or was already deleted.
142623.markdown: Fixed a race condition in `kube-scheduler` async preemption where a preemptor pod could remain stuck in the unschedulable queue if its last victim pod was already deleted before the preemption API call executed. Changed the boolean return value of `preemption.Executor.PreemptPod` in `pkg/scheduler/framework/preemption` to return `true` when the API server deletes a bound victim (and will emit a pod deletion event), and `false` when the victim was preempted only in scheduler memory or was already deleted. ([#142623](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/142623), [@wasylkowski-a](https://github.com/wasylkowski-a)) [SIG Scheduling and Testing]
142623.author: wasylkowski-a
142623.pr_body:
#### What type of PR is this?

/kind bug
/kind flake
/sig scheduling

#### What this PR does / why we need it:

In async preemption (KEP: https://github.com/kubernetes/enhancements/issues/4832), `PreEnqueue` only checks the last victim in `lastVictimsPendingPreemption` to determine when preemption has completed. When multiple preemptors target overlapping victim sets on the same node (or a victim is deleted concurrently), a preemptor's last victim can be deleted and its `AssignedPodDelete` event processed while the preemptor is still evicting preceding victims in `Parallelizer().Until` (before `lastVictimsPendingPreemption` is populated). When `PreemptPod` subsequently attempts to patch or delete that last victim and receives `NotFound`, no pod deletion event will follow, leaving the preemptor stuck in the unschedulable pod pool.

This PR updates `PreemptPod` to return `true, nil` only when the API server deletes a bound victim and will emit a pod deletion event, and `false, nil` when no deletion event will follow (when the victim is preempted in memory or when `PatchPodStatus` or `DeletePod` returns `NotFound`), ensuring `prepareCandidateAsync` activates the preemptor once its `preempting` state is cleared.

AI was used to assist in preparing and verifying these changes, and the author carefully reviewed the code before creating the PR.

#### Which issue(s) this PR fixes:

Fixes #142590

#### Special notes for your reviewer:

#### Does this PR introduce a user-facing change?

```release-note
Fixed a race condition in `kube-scheduler` async preemption where a preemptor pod could remain stuck in the unschedulable queue if its last victim pod was already deleted before the preemption API call executed.
Changed the boolean return value of `preemption.Executor.PreemptPod` in `pkg/scheduler/framework/preemption` to return `true` when the API server deletes a bound victim (and will emit a pod deletion event), and `false` when the victim was preempted only in scheduler memory or was already deleted.
```

#### What this PR does / why we need it:

Path validation for `--allowlist-entry` is inconsistent between saving and loading kuberc. The setter performs less validation than the loader, allowing it to save a configuration that kubectl subsequently rejects.

Starting with a valid kuberc file, the following command succeeds without this fix:

```
kubectl kuberc set --kuberc ~/.kube/kuberc --section credentialplugin --policy Allowlist --allowlist-entry command=./credential-helper
```

However, a subsequent command fails before querying any Pods:

```
# kubectl --kuberc ~/.kube/kuberc get pods
...
error occurred while applying preferences non-normalized file path: "./credential-helper" vs "credential-helper"
```

When loading kuberc, kubectl compares each allowlist entry with its normalized path:

```
Stored path:     ./credential-helper
Normalized path: credential-helper
```

Because these differ, kubectl reports `non-normalized file path` and exits before executing the requested command. It does not automatically normalize the saved configuration.

The issue is not that `./program-name` is inherently invalid, nor that all relative paths are prohibited. Rather, kuberc requires allowlist paths to be already normalized, but the setter does not enforce that requirement.

The fix applies the same credential plugin policy validation before saving. Invalid entries are rejected immediately, leaving the existing configuration unchanged.

#### What this PR does / why we need it:

To route `foo.com/a` to service `svc` on named port `http`, use  `--rule='foo.com/a=svc:http'` 

If a user enters an invalid rule such as:

```
kubectl create ingress demo --rule='foo.com/a=b=svc:http'
```

the command incorrectly accepts it. Instead of returning a clear validation error, `kubectl` later prints a Go array-out-of-bounds stack trace.

```
panic: runtime error: index out of range [1] with length 1
```

During Ingress construction, the rule is split on `=` into:

```
["a", "b", "svc:http"]
```

The code expects the second element to contain complete service configuration in `service-name:port` format, but it gets `b`. It then attempts to parse a service port from `b`. Since `b` contains no `:`, splitting it produces only one element, while code still accesses second element for port. This causes an array-out-of-bounds panic in local `kubectl` process.

Expected behavior: any `--rule` whose path contains an extra `=` or `,` must be rejected as invalid input before Ingress construction begins.

142665.text: Fixed `FileKeyRef` handling in `kubelet` to honor `optional: true` when the env file does not exist, publishing a key with an empty value (`KEY=''`) instead of reporting it as missing. Additionally, a value after whitespace following `=` in an env file (such as `KEY= 'value'`) causes a parse error instead of being read as an empty value.
142665.markdown: Fixed `FileKeyRef` handling in `kubelet` to honor `optional: true` when the env file does not exist, publishing a key with an empty value (`KEY=''`) instead of reporting it as missing. Additionally, a value after whitespace following `=` in an env file (such as `KEY= 'value'`) causes a parse error instead of being read as an empty value. ([#142665](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/142665), [@imusmanmalik](https://github.com/imusmanmalik)) [SIG Node and Testing]
142665.author: imusmanmalik
142665.pr_body:
#### What type of PR is this?

/kind bug
/sig node

#### What this PR does / why we need it:

`FileKeyRef` ignores `optional` when the env file does not exist, and reports a key with an empty value as missing, leaving the container in `CreateContainerConfigError` in both cases. Both come from `ParseEnv` returning only `(string, error)`, which leaves the caller using an empty return value as its not-found sentinel and returning on the open error before it checks `optional`.

`ParseEnv` now also returns whether the key was found, and the caller skips the variable when the file is absent and the reference is optional. The `ConfigMapKeyRef` branch in the same function already distinguishes these cases this way, using the `ok` value from the map lookup.

Only a missing file is treated as skippable. Permission errors, `ENOTDIR`, read failures and syntax errors still fail the container, which matches the ConfigMap and Secret paths where only `IsNotFound` is tolerated.

`ParseEnv` now also rejects `KEY= 'val'`. That line used to be read as an empty value, and the code comment said this matched bash, but bash ends the assignment at the whitespace and runs `val` as a command. Whitespace after `=` followed by nothing or by a comment, as in `KEY=   ` or `KEY= # comment`, still assigns an empty value, as it does in bash. Any other content after that whitespace fails with `unexpected content after whitespace following '='`. Like the existing whitespace-before-`=` check, the error fires for any line the parser reads before it finds the requested key.

#### Which issue(s) this PR is related to:

Fixes #142662

#### Special notes for your reviewer:

`ParseEnv` gains a `found` return. It has one production caller and one test in tree, both updated here. The similarly named `ParseEnv` in `staging/src/k8s.io/kubectl/pkg/cmd/set/env` is a different function and is untouched.

Unit tests:

- `TestMakeEnvironmentVariablesWithFileKeyRef` has five new cases. A missing file with `optional` and a key with an empty value fail before this change with `couldn't parse env file` and `environment variable key "EMPTY" not found in file`. A key written as `EMPTY= # comment` must be published as an empty value. A file containing `DATABASE= 'db'`, referenced with `optional` unset and set, must fail in both cases.
- `TestParseEnv` has eight new cases for the text after `=`. The old parser accepts `KEY1= 'val1'` (for that key and for a later one) and `KEY1= val1`, so those cases fail on it with `expected error, got none`. `KEY1=#x` must also fail, as it already did, because bash reads it as the value `#x`. `KEY1=   `, `KEY1= # comment` and a tab followed by a comment must give an empty value, and a later key in the same file must still be found. These empty cases run through the existing `bash --posix` cross-check. A `wantNotFound` field keeps the empty-value and absent-key cases apart.

e2e tests in `test/e2e/common/node/file_key.go`:

- `should handle optional missing file or key` now also references a file that is never written, so it covers what its name says.
- `should publish a key with an empty value` checks that `EMPTY_KEY=''` reaches the container as an empty variable.
- `should fail when the file has invalid syntax even if the key is optional` checks that `BAD_KEY= 'value'` still ends in `CreateContainerConfigError`.

I ran the `FileKeyRef` e2e tests (`e2e.test --provider=skeleton --ginkgo.focus=FileKeyRef`) on two kind clusters. On a node image built from this branch, all 14 pass. On stock `kindest/node:v1.37.0`, 11 pass and these three fail: the missing-file and empty-value pods stay in `CreateContainerConfigError` with `couldn't parse env file` and `environment variable key "EMPTY_KEY" not found in file`, and the invalid-syntax pod starts, because the old parser read `BAD_KEY= 'value'` as an empty value.

Verified on linux/arm64 with golang:1.27: `go test -race ./pkg/kubelet/util/env/`, `go test ./pkg/kubelet/ ./pkg/kubelet/util/...`, `go vet` (including `./test/e2e/common/node/`) and `gofmt`, all clean. The two pod specs in the issue reproduce the old behaviour on stock v1.36.1 and v1.37.0 clusters.

I have not opened backports. `EnvFiles` is default-on in 1.35 through 1.37, and I am happy to prepare cherry-picks if sig-node wants them.

/cc @HirazawaUi @SergeyKanzhelev

#### Does this PR introduce a user-facing change?

```release-note
kubelet: FileKeyRef now honors `optional: true` when the env file does not exist, and publishes a key with an empty value (`KEY=''`) instead of reporting it as missing. A value after whitespace following `=` in an env file, as in `KEY= 'value'`, is now a parse error instead of being read as an empty value.
```

142702.text: Promoted the `ShardedListAndWatch` feature gate to Beta.
142702.markdown: Promoted the `ShardedListAndWatch` feature gate to Beta. ([#142702](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/142702), [@Jefftree](https://github.com/Jefftree)) [SIG API Machinery and Testing]
142702.author: Jefftree
142702.pr_body:
#### What type of PR is this?

/kind feature

#### What this PR does / why we need it:

Graduates the `ShardedListAndWatch` feature gate to Beta.

Tested 10,000 Pods (~2.7 KB each) across 10 `kube-state-metrics` shards:

|Metric|Client-Side|Server-Side|Delta|
|---|---:|---:|---:|
|apiserver watch events|100,027|10,012|-90%|
|apiserver CPU|11.0s|1.2s|-89%|
|apiserver heap allocs|600 MiB|78 MiB|-87%|
|apiserver RSS growth|+77 MiB|+16 MiB|-79%|
|kube-state-metrics CPU (per shard)|1.07s|0.31s|-71%|
|kube-state-metrics heap allocs (per shard)|113 MiB|44 MiB|-61%|

I am actually quite surprised by the result. Sharding is expected to reduce events and help on the controller side, but apiserver actually benefits significantly. 

Projected benefits are lower CPU + heap allocs per client shard, and better memory utilization. Secondary benefits include reduced network cost.

In theory, the incremental cost of a watcher shouldn't be that high. Unfortunately for WatchList we deepcopy every init event which leads to duplicate work per object during an initial list. As a result sharding performs provides a significant improvement to apiserver load as well during initialization and reconnects. This is a watchlist bug that is being tracked that currently makes sharding results look really great on the apiserver.

#### Which issue(s) this PR is related to:

KEP: https://github.com/kubernetes/enhancements/issues/5866

142719.pr_body:
> [!NOTE]
> This PR is copied from original PR https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/142375 by @macsko while the author is on leave, in order to finish review and merge it. It includes @macsko's commit plus a follow-up commit fixing CPG preemption integration test setups (`preemption_test.go`) where child `PodGroup`s were missing `DisruptionModeAll()`.

#### What type of PR is this?

/kind feature

#### What this PR does / why we need it:

This PR adds more validation steps to pod group cycle in kube-scheduler to enforce the cases where:
 - the hierarchy does not exceed WorkloadMaxTreeDepth (and has no CompositePodGroup at depth WorkloadMaxTreeDepth),
 - all groups in the hierarchy reference the same Workload as the root group,
 - no gang parent group has a basic child group,
 - no parent group with All disruption mode has a child group with Single disruption mode.

It implements the decision from CPG KEP (https://github.com/kubernetes/enhancements/issues/6012).

KEP: https://github.com/kubernetes/enhancements/issues/6012

Copied from #142375. A follow-up commit was added to configure `.DisruptionModeAll()` on child `PodGroup`s in `test/integration/scheduler/preemption/preemption_test.go`, fixing integration test failures caused by API defaulting.

142761.text: Fixed an issue where `kubelet` lost a Pod's failure phase and reason when containers exited successfully during eviction, `kubelet` preemption, or graceful node shutdown.
142761.markdown: Fixed an issue where `kubelet` lost a Pod's failure phase and reason when containers exited successfully during eviction, `kubelet` preemption, or graceful node shutdown. ([#142761](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/142761), [@amrmahdi](https://github.com/amrmahdi)) [SIG Node and Testing]
142761.author: amrmahdi
142761.pr_body:
#### What type of PR is this?

/kind bug

#### What this PR does / why we need it:

When the kubelet terminates a pod with a failure status (eviction, critical-pod preemption, graceful node shutdown) and the container handles SIGTERM by exiting 0, the pod ends up `Succeeded` with an empty reason. The caller's status override sets `Phase=Failed` and the reason in the status manager cache, but that update is withheld while containers may still be running, and `generateAPIPodStatus` later recomputes `Succeeded` from the exit code. Because the recomputed phase differs from the cached one, the reason and message are dropped too.

Per the discussion with @tallclair on the issue, this does two things:

- `SyncTerminatingPod` re-applies the caller's status override to the status it generates after the containers have stopped, which is the update the status manager is allowed to publish as terminal.
- `generateAPIPodStatus` no longer lets a pod move from `Failed` to `Succeeded`. A `Failed` phase already recorded wins over a `Succeeded` phase computed from exit codes alone. `Succeeded` to `Failed` remains allowed in the cached status; a terminal phase already published to the API server is still protected by the existing illegal-transition check.

#### Which issue(s) this PR is related to:

Fixes #141483

#### Special notes for your reviewer:

The override is applied at both status updates rather than moved; the first application is harmless with the merge guard in place. Each hunk is covered independently: reverting only the `SyncTerminatingPod` change fails the new termination test on the override count, reverting only the merge change fails it on phase and conditions.

Verified end to end on kind with the same emptyDir `sizeLimit` eviction repro, container exiting 0 on SIGTERM: stock `kindest/node:v1.37.0` reports `Succeeded` with no reason (3/3), a node image built from this branch reports `Failed / Evicted` with the message (3/3).

This does not cover a kubelet restart before the terminal status reaches the API server, where the cached decision is lost. That gap exists today for every eviction and is not widened here; it would need a durable marker on the pod object and is left for a follow-up.

AI assistance (Claude) was used to draft the change and tests. I reviewed the code, ran the kubelet, status, eviction, preemption and node-shutdown test suites, and verified the behaviour on kind.

#### Does this PR introduce a user-facing change?

```release-note
Fixed the kubelet losing a pod's failure phase and reason when its containers exited successfully during eviction, kubelet preemption, or graceful node shutdown.
```

142763.text: kube-apiserver: Fixed a race during graceful shutdown that let active watch requests close without the rate limiting configured by `--shutdown-watch-termination-grace-period`. With many open watches, a large share of them could close at once, causing their clients to reconnect at the same time.
142763.markdown: Kube-apiserver: Fixed a race during graceful shutdown that let active watch requests close without the rate limiting configured by `--shutdown-watch-termination-grace-period`. With many open watches, a large share of them could close at once, causing their clients to reconnect at the same time. ([#142763](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/142763), [@emanolios-stripe](https://github.com/emanolios-stripe))
142763.author: emanolios-stripe
142763.pr_body:
#### What type of PR is this?

/kind bug

#### What this PR does / why we need it:

With `--shutdown-watch-termination-grace-period` > 0, active watch requests return as soon as `NotAcceptingNewRequest` is signaled. The drain goroutine wakes on the same signal and only then calls `WatchRequestWaitGroup.Wait`, which installs the rate limiter. A watch whose deferred `Done()` runs before `Wait` is not rate limited, so with many watches a large share of them can be closed at once. That is the thundering herd the grace period was added to prevent.

This PR adds an `WatchRequestsDraining` lifecycle signal and exposes it through `ServerShutdownSignal.DrainingWatches()`. Watch handlers use this accessor through `WatchServer.DrainWatchCh` to begin returning. 

The lifecycle order is:
`NotAcceptingNewRequest` → `WatchRequestsDraining` → `InFlightRequestsDrained`.

Tests:
- `TestGracefulTerminationWatchShutdownOrdering` opens 200 watch requests and checks that the watch waitgroup has entered waiting mode when each handler observes `DrainingWatches()`. It also checks that `ShuttingDown()` is signaled before draining starts.
- `TestRateLimitedSafeWaitGroupSignalFromFactory` verifies that `Done()` calls following a notification from the factory use the limiter, and that positive `Add()` calls are rejected. The factory's locking contract is also documented on `RateLimiterFactoryFunc`.

#### Which issue(s) this PR is related to:

Fixes #142749

#### Special notes for your reviewer:

- The signal fires with `RateLimitedSafeWaitGroup.mu` held. The notification closes a channel; the factory does not wait for the woken handlers.
- The meaning of `ShuttingDown()` is unchanged.

#### Does this PR introduce a user-facing change?

```release-note
kube-apiserver: fixed a race during graceful shutdown that let active watch requests close without the rate limiting configured by `--shutdown-watch-termination-grace-period`.
```

#### AI usage disclosure:

YES. Claude helped investigate the race, write the reproducing test and the fix, and draft this description. I reviewed and tested the change and take responsibility for it.

142777.text: Fixed a bug in kube-scheduler where the `PodGroupInitiallyScheduled` or `CompositePodGroupInitiallyScheduled` condition of a PodGroup or CompositePodGroup could be overwritten from `True` to `False` by a scheduling cycle that ran before the scheduler observed its own status update.
142777.markdown: Fixed a bug in kube-scheduler where the `PodGroupInitiallyScheduled` or `CompositePodGroupInitiallyScheduled` condition of a PodGroup or CompositePodGroup could be overwritten from `True` to `False` by a scheduling cycle that ran before the scheduler observed its own status update. ([#142777](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/142777), [@rithwik-01](https://github.com/rithwik-01)) [SIG Scheduling and Testing]
142777.author: rithwik-01
142777.pr_body:
#### What type of PR is this?

/kind flake
/kind bug

#### What this PR does / why we need it:

`TestCPGScheduling/TestCPGBasicWithGangChildren` and `TestCPGScheduling/TestCPGMinGroupCount` flake because a PodGroup's or CompositePodGroup's `InitiallyScheduled=True` condition can be overwritten with `False` right after the scheduler writes it.

The status patch is computed from the scheduler cache, which doesn't see the scheduler's own write until the watch event arrives. A later cycle of the same hierarchy in that window passes the "don't regress a True condition" check and patches `False` over `True`. Root cause: https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/issues/142677#issuecomment-6123966986

Fix (design from https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/issues/142677#issuecomment-6270727119):

- After the `True` status patch succeeds, the scheduler records in the group's cache state that it set the condition to `True`. A failed patch records nothing, so the cache never claims a `True` the API server doesn't have. If the record or the cached condition is `True`, the group is already initially scheduled and its condition is not updated again (no regression to `False`, no redundant `True`->`True` patches).
- The record holds the group's UID, so a deleted and recreated group with the same name is unaffected. It lives in `podGroupState` / `compositePodGroupState`, so informer updates don't change it and snapshots don't copy it.
- New internal `Cache` methods: `AssumeGroupInitiallyScheduled` and `IsGroupInitiallyScheduled`.
- `updatePodGroupCondition` and `updateCompositePodGroupCondition` are merged into `updateInitiallyScheduledCondition`, which builds the condition itself and infers its type from the group. NotFound on the patch is logged at V(4) instead of as an error.
- Re-enables the `WaitForGroupsScheduled` checks disabled by #143181.

#### Which issue(s) this PR is related to:

https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/issues/142677

#### Special notes for your reviewer:

- New `Test*InitiallyScheduledConditionStaleCache` tests reproduce the interleaving; the `True is not regressed` case fails on master and passes here. `TestAssumeGroupInitiallyScheduled` and `TestIsGroupInitiallyScheduled` cover the cache methods.
- Earlier verification, before this review revision: with the checks re-enabled, the two flaking tests failed 6/420 runs under CPU load on master's scheduler code and 0/420 with the prior revision of this PR.
- Verification of this revision: the full scheduler and cache unit suites passed; the affected `InitiallyScheduled` tests passed under the race detector; both original flaky integration cases passed three runs each. `go vet`, formatting, and whitespace checks passed. Temporary mutations removing the assumption, moving it before the patch, or restoring True->True updates each failed the expected regression tests.
- In earlier integration runs, `TestCPGTopologyAwareScheduling/...PodGroupPodsCount_placement_scoring` timed out on both master (4/20) and the prior PR revision (3/20), indicating a separate issue.
- AI assistance was used for code review, verification, and preparing this PR update. The human author is responsible for the submitted changes.

#### Does this PR introduce a user-facing change?

```release-note
Fixed a bug in kube-scheduler where a PodGroup's or CompositePodGroup's InitiallyScheduled=True condition could be overwritten with False by a scheduling cycle that ran before the scheduler observed its own status update.
```
