142823.text: Fixed a bug in fake client-go's object tracker where deletions that occurred between an initial List and subsequent Watch were lost.
142823.markdown: Fixed a bug in fake client-go's object tracker where deletions that occurred between an initial List and subsequent Watch were lost. ([#142823](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/142823), [@bodapatisaikrishna](https://github.com/bodapatisaikrishna))
142823.author: bodapatisaikrishna
142823.pr_body:
#### What type of PR is this?

/kind bug
/sig api-machinery
/area client-go

#### What this PR does / why we need it:

In client-go's fake tracker, `Watch(opts)` replays existing objects when starting at an earlier resource version, but deletions occurring between an initial `List` and subsequent `Watch` were dropped because deleted objects are removed from `t.objects` and deletions did not advance `resourceVersions`. Informer caches would then retain deleted objects indefinitely.

This PR:
- Assigns a resource version to deletions and retains the last 100 deletions per GVR in a bounded history buffer.
- Replays matching deletions when a watch starts at an older resource version.
- Emits a resource expired error event if the requested version is older than retained history or if pending events exceed watcher buffer capacity, allowing the reflector to relist.
- Adds unit and deterministic synctest tests covering deletions between List and Watch.

#### Which issue(s) this PR is related to:

Fixes #141528

#### Special notes for your reviewer:

cc @pohly

Fixed a bug in fake client-go's object tracker where deletions that occurred between an initial List and subsequent Watch were lost.
```

142842.text: Fixed a bug where kubelet was killing containers one at a time when restarting them without deleting the pod.
142842.markdown: Fixed a bug where kubelet was killing containers one at a time when restarting them without deleting the pod. ([#142842](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/142842), [@adamwathieu](https://github.com/adamwathieu)) [SIG Node and Testing]
142842.author: adamwathieu
142842.pr_body:
#### What type of PR is this?

/kind bug
/sig node

#### What this PR does / why we need it:

When a kubelet pod goroutine needs to kill containers without killing the pod sandbox (for example, kubectl set image), SyncPod() kills those containers one at a time. This becomes a problem because a long PreStop hook makes the subsequent containers have to wait, and delays the rest of the reconciliation loop.

Kill the containers concurrently instead, sharing the logic that is already used to kill containers in parallel when the whole pod is torn down.

Note that this changes how container kill errors are handled. Previously, SyncPod() would return on the first failed kill without attempting to kill the remaining containers. Now, it tries every container and records all the results before returning.

I measured the change on a kind cluster, running the script below against a kubelet built before and after this PR. Each cell shows the seconds from updating every container's image until all of the pod's containers are running and Ready, as P50 / P90 / max over 16 trials for each row.

| Containers | preStop | Before (serial) | After (concurrent) |
| ---: | --- | ---: | ---: |
| 2 | none | 2.20 / 2.25 / 2.26 | 2.18 / 2.22 / 2.23 |
| 2 | `sleep 5` | 12.31 / 12.37 / 12.41 | 7.23 / 7.26 / 7.30 |
| 8 | none | 3.47 / 3.53 / 3.55 | 3.16 / 3.22 / 3.25 |
| 8 | `sleep 5` | 43.99 / 44.09 / 44.13 | 8.26 / 8.34 / 8.36 |

<details>
<summary>Reproduction script</summary>

```bash
#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Times in-place restarts of all of a pod's containers.
#
# For each container count and preStop hook, the script creates a pod, waits
# until it's Ready, then changes every container's image from its tag to the
# same image by digest. That changes each container's spec hash, so the kubelet
# kills all of the containers in one sync and starts them again (no new
# sandbox, no image pull). It prints the seconds from the image change until
# every container is running again and Ready.
#
# Usage: ./restart_bench.sh | tee results.csv
set -euo pipefail

TRIALS=16
CONTAINERS="2 8"
PRESTOP_SECONDS="0 5"  # 0: no preStop hook.
IMAGE=registry.k8s.io/e2e-test-images/busybox:1.37.0-2
STATUS='{{range .status.containerStatuses}}{{.restartCount}}{{.ready}} {{end}}{{"\n"}}'

pod_yaml() {  # NAME CONTAINERS PRESTOP_SECONDS
  cat <<EOF
apiVersion: v1
kind: Pod
metadata:
  name: $1
  labels: {app: restart-bench}
spec:
  terminationGracePeriodSeconds: $(($3 + 10))
  containers:
EOF
  for i in $(seq "$2"); do
    cat <<EOF
  - name: c$i
    image: $IMAGE
    command: ["sh", "-c", "trap 'exit 0' TERM; sleep 2147483647 & wait"]
EOF
    if (($3 > 0)); then
      echo "    lifecycle: {preStop: {exec: {command: [sleep, \"$3\"]}}}"
    fi
  done
}

kubectl delete pod -l app=restart-bench >/dev/null  # Left from an earlier run.
trap 'kubectl delete pod -l app=restart-bench --wait=false >/dev/null 2>&1' EXIT

echo "containers,prestop_s,trial,seconds"
for n in $CONTAINERS; do
  for prestop in $PRESTOP_SECONDS; do
    for trial in $(seq "$TRIALS"); do
      pod=restart-bench-$n-$prestop-$trial
      pod_yaml "$pod" "$n" "$prestop" | kubectl create -f - >/dev/null
      kubectl wait --for=condition=Ready "pod/$pod" --timeout=2m >/dev/null
      digest=$(kubectl get pod "$pod" -o jsonpath='{.status.containerStatuses[0].imageID}')
      want=$(printf '1true %.0s' $(seq "$n"))  # restartCount 1 and Ready, per container
      want=${want% }
      start=

      while read -r line; do
        if [[ -z $start ]]; then  # The first line is the pod before the change.
          kubectl set image "pod/$pod" "*=$digest" >/dev/null
          start=$(date +%s%N)
        elif [[ $line == "$want" ]]; then
          break
        fi
      done < <(timeout 5m kubectl get pods --field-selector "metadata.name=$pod" \
        --watch -o go-template="$STATUS")
      ms=$((($(date +%s%N) - ${start:-0}) / 1000000))

      if [[ $line == "$want" ]]; then
        echo "$n,$prestop,$trial,$((ms / 1000)).$(printf '%03d' $((ms % 1000)))"
      else
        echo "$n,$prestop,$trial,FAILED"
      fi
      kubectl delete pod "$pod" >/dev/null
    done
  done
done
```
</details>

#### Which issue(s) this PR is related to:

Related to WIP KEP https://github.com/kubernetes/enhancements/pull/6419, in particular https://github.com/kubernetes/enhancements/pull/6419/changes#r4210404546

142902.pr_body:
Deployment rollouts fail to report timeouts after old ReplicaSet scale-down errors

5. If the PR is unfinished, see how to mark it: https://git.k8s.io/community/contributors/guide/pull-requests.md#marking-unfinished-pull-requests
-->

#### What type of PR is this?

/kind bug

<!--
Add one of the following kinds:
/kind bug
/kind dependency
/kind cleanup
/kind documentation
/kind feature

Optionally add one or more of the following kinds if applicable:
/kind api-change
/kind deprecation
/kind failing-test
/kind flake
/kind regression
-->

#### What this PR does / why we need it:

For example, a user updates a Deployment's image to start a rolling update. Once the new replicas have reached their currently permitted limit, the next step is to scale down the old ReplicaSet. If the admission webhook that validates ReplicaSet updates repeatedly fails, and kube-apiserver rejects the update requests. The old ReplicaSet therefore cannot be scaled down, and the rollout stops progressing.

After the rollout has made no progress for `progressDeadlineSeconds`, the Deployment's `Progressing` condition should become `False` with reason `ProgressDeadlineExceeded`. `kubectl rollout status` should report a rollout timeout and exit. 

Before this fix, however, each sync returned early after the scale-down failure and skipped both the rollout status update and the timeout check. As a result, the `Progressing` condition remained `True`. With default settings, `kubectl rollout status` kept waiting for the rollout to complete while the failure persisted.

```
func (dc *DeploymentController) reconcileOldReplicaSets(...) (bool, error) {
    ...
    oldRSs, cleanupCount, err := dc.cleanupUnhealthyReplicas(ctx, oldRSs, deployment, maxScaledDown)
    if err != nil {
        // The PR now propagates the scale-down error to the caller.
        return false, err
    }
}

func (dc *DeploymentController) rolloutRolling(ctx context.Context, d *apps.Deployment, rsList []*apps.ReplicaSet) error {
    ...
    // Scale down, if we can.
    scaledDown, err := dc.reconcileOldReplicaSets(ctx, allRSs, controller.FilterActiveReplicaSets(oldRSs), newRS, d)
    if err != nil {
        // Return immediately on error.
        // Rollout status updates and timeout checks are skipped.
        return err
    }
    ...
}
```

This fix ensures that the controller still updates the rollout status and checks for a timeout after a scale-down failure. It then returns the scale-down error to trigger a retry.

([#142908](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/142908), [@tanishbhandari11t](https://github.com/tanishbhandari11t)) [SIG Cloud Provider and Instrumentation]
142908.author: tanishbhandari11t
142908.pr_body:
#### What type of PR is this?

/kind bug

#### What this PR does / why we need it:

cloud-controller-manager registers the `NativeHistograms` feature gate but never calls `metricsfeatures.ApplyFeatureGates`, so enabling the gate has no effect and all histograms stay classic-only. Since the gate is Beta and on by default in 1.37, cloud-controller-manager currently reports the gate as enabled while not exposing native histograms.

This calls `ApplyFeatureGates` before `Config()` in both command entry points, `NewCloudControllerManagerCommand` and `CommandBuilder.BuildCommand`, matching kube-controller-manager, kube-scheduler, kubelet and kube-proxy.

#### Which issue(s) this PR is related to:

Fixes #142454

#### Special notes for your reviewer:

The unit test runs both commands with `--feature-gates=NativeHistograms=true` and checks that newly created histograms are native. It fails without the fix.

I did not add a case to `test/integration/metrics/nativehistograms`: those tests start kube-apiserver in the same process, which already applies the gate process-wide, so a cloud-controller-manager case there would pass without the fix.

142922.text: Fixed an issue where Job `status.ready` decreased when deleting a Ready Pod failed.
142922.markdown: Fixed an issue where Job `status.ready` decreased when deleting a Ready Pod failed. ([#142922](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/142922), [@yankovitchg](https://github.com/yankovitchg))
142922.author: yankovitchg
142922.pr_body:
#### What type of PR is this?

/kind bug

#### What this PR does / why we need it:

When the Job controller deletes pods, it also adjusts `status.ready` by counting how many of those pods were Ready. Two helpers did that incorrectly when `DeletePod` failed:

- `deleteActivePods` (Job failed / finished: delete remaining active pods) always counted a Ready pod toward `deletedReady`, even if the delete errored.
- `deleteJobPods` (scale-down when over parallelism, suspend, etc.: patch tracking finalizer then delete) did the same after a failed `DeletePod`.

Callers then subtract that count from `jobCtx.ready`, so a failed delete could undercount Ready until a later sync corrected it.

This PR only decrements Ready when the delete actually succeeded (or the pod was already gone / `NotFound`).

#### Which issue(s) this PR is related to:

N/A

#### Special notes for your reviewer:

- `deleteActivePods`: Ready increment moved into the success branch (`else if`).
- `deleteJobPods`: Ready increment gated on `err == nil || apierrors.IsNotFound(err)` (same success notion as the delete path).
- Tests: `FakePodControl.DeleteErr` so Patch can succeed while Delete fails (needed for `deleteJobPods`). New `TestControllerSyncJob` cases for scale-down and job-fail paths.

/sig apps

142938.text: client-go: Added the `MinConnectionPoolSize` field to `rest.Config` and `transport.Config`. When it is greater than 1, the client spreads requests across at least that many connections to the server and sends each request to a connection with fewer requests in flight. This helps when a single load balancer fronts multiple API server backends. Clients that do not set the field are not affected. The beta `ClientsAllowConnectionPool` client-go feature gate controls this behavior and is enabled by default. To disable it, set `KUBE_FEATURE_ClientsAllowConnectionPool=false`.
142938.markdown: Client-go: Added the `MinConnectionPoolSize` field to `rest.Config` and `transport.Config`. When it is greater than 1, the client spreads requests across at least that many connections to the server and sends each request to a connection with fewer requests in flight. This helps when a single load balancer fronts multiple API server backends. Clients that do not set the field are not affected. The beta `ClientsAllowConnectionPool` client-go feature gate controls this behavior and is enabled by default. To disable it, set `KUBE_FEATURE_ClientsAllowConnectionPool=false`. ([#142938](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/142938), [@mborsz](https://github.com/mborsz))
142938.author: mborsz
142938.pr_body:
#### What type of PR is this?
/kind feature

#### What this PR does / why we need it:
This PR adds a support for a new client-go level configuration `MinConnectionPoolSize` that can be used to force creating at least `MinConnectionPoolSize` connections to the same endpoint. The valid use case of this would be: having single load balancer that is backed by multiple backends.

Once connected, the requests are routed based on power of two choices for in-flight requests.

In the next PR I will add changes to the kubeconfig types and similar way to make it easier to enable by changing kubeconfig. For sake of simplifying review, sending this first to unblock in-code opt-in.

The feature is explicitly opt-in, there is no impact on clients that do not plan to use it.
It can be safely disabled by disabling the ClientsAllowConnectionPool client-go feature gate, which restores single-connection behaviour, even if client opted-in.

Existing per-connection MaxConcurrentStream vs this pool mechanism interaction: The initial version implements option "overflow" from https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/issues/142383#issuecomment-5929081955 We can adjust this if we find this too simple. The field is intentionally named `MinConnectionPoolSize` not `ConnectionPoolSize`, so we that have a freedom of creating more connections if necessary, e.g. for option "mixed".

#### Which issue(s) this PR is related to:
https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/issues/142383


#### Special notes for your reviewer:
Commits are meant to be reviewed one by one. The pool is cached in the TLS transport cache as a single entry, so re-creating clients for the same config (including same `MinConnectionPoolSize`) will return the same transport and connections (covered by unit test).

#### Does this PR introduce a user-facing change?
<!--
If no, just write "NONE" in the release-note block below.
If yes, a release note is required:
Enter your extended release note in the block below. If the PR requires additional action from users switching to the new release, include the string "action required".

For more information on release notes see: https://git.k8s.io/community/contributors/guide/release-notes.md
-->
```release-note
client-go: added `MinConnectionPoolSize` to `rest.Config` and `transport.Config`. When greater than 1, requests to the server are spread across at least that many independent connections, preferring the one with fewer requests in flight. 142950.text: Fixed `kube-scheduler` handling of PodGroup and CompositePodGroup objects deleted and recreated under the same name during a watch interruption, processing them as a deletion followed by an addition rather than an in-place update to keep the cache and queue hierarchy consistent.
142950.markdown: Fixed `kube-scheduler` handling of PodGroup and CompositePodGroup objects deleted and recreated under the same name during a watch interruption, processing them as a deletion followed by an addition rather than an in-place update to keep the cache and queue hierarchy consistent. ([#142950](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/142950), [@divyanshuprakas-h](https://github.com/divyanshuprakas-h))
142950.author: divyanshuprakas-h
142950.pr_body:
#### What type of PR is this?

/kind bug

#### What this PR does / why we need it:

- Fixes scheduler event handling for `PodGroup` and `CompositePodGroup` objects that are deleted and recreated with the same namespace and name.
- Kubernetes informers may coalesce a deletion and subsequent recreation into a single update notification.
- In this scenario, the old and new objects have the same namespace and name but different UIDs, representing different object instances.
- Previously, the scheduler's update handlers treated these notifications as ordinary updates instead of explicitly removing the old object and adding the replacement.
- Updates `updatePodGroup` and `updateCompositePodGroup` to compare the UIDs of the old and new objects.
- When the UIDs differ, the handlers process the event as a deletion of the old object followed by an addition of the new object.
- Preserves the existing update behavior when both objects have the same UID.
- Retains the resource-version equality check for same-UID objects, while ensuring a UID mismatch takes precedence over that check.
- Preserves event-handling metric semantics by recording replacement events through the delete and add handlers rather than as ordinary updates.
- Adds regression tests for both resource types, covering replacement scenarios with different UIDs.

#### Which issue(s) this PR is related to:

Fixes #142930

#### Special notes for your reviewer:

- The change is limited to scheduler event handling for `PodGroup` and `CompositePodGroup` resources.
- Objects with matching UIDs continue through the existing update path, including the resource-version no-op check.
- Objects with different UIDs are handled as a deletion of the old object followed by an addition of the new object.
- Regression tests cover replacement events for both resource types.
- No public API or resource schema changes are introduced.
- Validation performed locally:
  - `go test ./pkg/scheduler -run 'Test(UpdatePodGroup|UpdateCompositePodGroup)$' -count=1`
  - `go test ./pkg/scheduler -count=1`
  - `git diff --check`
- All listed tests passed locally.

#### Does this PR introduce a user-facing change?

```release-note
kube-scheduler: PodGroup and CompositePodGroup objects that are deleted and recreated under the same name while the scheduler's watch is interrupted are now processed as a deletion followed by an addition rather than an in-place update, keeping the scheduler's cache and queue hierarchy consistent.
```

143077.text: Fixed a kube-apiserver goroutine and memory leak: a watch-list (sendInitialEvents=true) watcher stayed blocked forever when the client disconnected while the watch cache closed the watcher as too slow.
143077.markdown: Fixed a kube-apiserver goroutine and memory leak: a watch-list (sendInitialEvents=true) watcher stayed blocked forever when the client disconnected while the watch cache closed the watcher as too slow. ([#143077](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/143077), [@nami-ant](https://github.com/nami-ant))
143077.author: nami-ant
143077.pr_body:
#### What type of PR is this?

/kind bug
/sig api-machinery

#### What this PR does / why we need it:

Fixes a watch cache goroutine leak:

1. The dispatcher blocks in `add` on a watch-list watcher whose bookmark is received but not sent.
2. The client stops the watch. `forget(false)` queues it in `watchersToStop`.
3. The time budget ends. `add` calls `forget(true)`, which turns draining on.
4. `stopLocked` leaves `done` open. The watcher goroutine blocks forever on the result channel.

Now each entry of `watchersToStop` keeps its own drain mode, and `finishDispatching` applies it just before `stopLocked`, as suggested in review. The non-draining stop closes `done`.

#### Which issue(s) this PR is related to:

Likely the cause of https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/issues/137631

Split out of kubernetes/kubernetes#141450 at the reviewer's request.

#### Special notes for your reviewer:

- Reach: the drain mechanism came with kubernetes/kubernetes#111460 (v1.25); both callers passed `false`. The first draining caller came with kubernetes/kubernetes#110960 (v1.27). The race needs a watch-list request.
- Related: kubernetes/kubernetes#141899 adds a 30s timeout to the initial-event send. In this race the goroutine is still sending initial events, so that timeout would end the leak after 30s. It does not stop a draining stop from overwriting a non-draining one.
- Trade-off: in this race `terminateAllWatchers` now closes a connected client at once, as documented. The client restarts its watch-list.
- Depends on https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/143640, which adds `TestWatchListStopDuringDispatch` and pins the leak. Only the second commit here is new. It holds the fix, flips the test to expect no leaked goroutine, and adds cases for `terminateAllWatchers` and for a watcher that still drains.

#### Does this PR introduce a user-facing change?

```release-note
Fixed a kube-apiserver goroutine and memory leak: a watch-list (sendInitialEvents=true) watcher stayed blocked forever when the client disconnected while the watch cache closed the watcher as too slow.
```

143087.text: Fixed an issue in `kubeadm` where automatic rollback of the etcd data directory after a failed etcd upgrade copied the backup into a subdirectory of the member directory instead of restoring it. The etcd backup directory contains the member directory contents, and etcd data backups before upgrades are retried for up to 30 seconds if copying fails.
143087.markdown: Fixed an issue in `kubeadm` where automatic rollback of the etcd data directory after a failed etcd upgrade copied the backup into a subdirectory of the member directory instead of restoring it. The etcd backup directory contains the member directory contents, and etcd data backups before upgrades are retried for up to 30 seconds if copying fails. ([#143087](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/143087), [@SEPURI-SAI-KRISHNA](https://github.com/SEPURI-SAI-KRISHNA))
143087.author: SEPURI-SAI-KRISHNA
143087.pr_body:
#### What type of PR is this?

/kind bug
/area kubeadm

#### What this PR does / why we need it:

When an etcd upgrade fails, kubeadm restores the etcd data dir from the backup it took before the upgrade. On Linux that restore never worked. The backup was `cp -r <dataDir> <backupDir>` into an already existing `<backupDir>`, so the data landed in `<backupDir>/<basename(dataDir)>`. The restore was `cp -r <backupDir> <dataDir>`, which copied the whole backup dir *inside* the live data dir and left the live data untouched, while kubeadm printed "Etcd data rollback successful".

- `CopyDir` is now one portable Go implementation in `copy.go`; the `cp` and `xcopy` variants in `copy_unix.go` and `copy_windows.go` are gone. It copies the contents of `src` into `dest` and keeps the source's file modes, so a restored etcd data dir stays 0700/0600.
- `rollbackEtcdData` removes `<dataDir>/member` before restoring, so files etcd wrote after the backup (WAL segments, snapshots) don't survive the rollback.
- The backup copies the data dir of a running etcd and can fail when etcd renames a WAL file mid-copy. It is now retried for up to 30 seconds, from an empty backup dir each time.

#### Which issue(s) this PR is related to:

Fixes kubernetes/kubeadm#3330
Fixes kubernetes/kubeadm#3324

#### Special notes for your reviewer:

- `CopyDir` walks `src` with `filepath.WalkDir` and reuses the existing `CopyFile`, which opens the destination with the source's mode and `O_TRUNC`. `os.CopyFS` was the obvious candidate but creates directories 0777 and files `0666|perm&0777` and refuses to overwrite (`O_CREATE|O_EXCL`), which would loosen the restored etcd data dir; see the discussion below.
- I checked the retry by making one file in the data dir unreadable: when the file goes away the backup succeeds on the next attempt, and when it doesn't the upgrade fails after 30 seconds with the underlying copy error.
- `rollbackEtcdData` now stats `<backupEtcdDir>/member` and returns before touching the live data dir if it isn't there, so a missing backup can't leave the node with neither. `TestRollbackEtcdData` covers both directions; without the guard its second case fails with `rollbackEtcdData() error = <nil>, wantErr true`.
- The `TestCopyDir/existing_destination` subtest copies into an already existing `dst`, as both the backup and the restore do, and checks that the contents land in `dst` and `src` isn't nested inside it. It fails on master on Linux and passes with this change.
- On Linux the backup layout changes from `<backupDir>/etcd/member` to `<backupDir>/member`, which is what Windows already did.

#### Does this PR introduce a user-facing change?

```release-note
kubeadm: fixed the automatic rollback of the etcd data directory after a failed etcd upgrade, which previously copied the backup into a subdirectory of the member directory instead of restoring where it should be. The etcd backup directory now holds the member directory's contents. The etcd data backup before an upgrade is now retried for up to 30 seconds if copying fails.
```

143103.text: Fixed an issue where the storage version migrator removed old versions from a CustomResourceDefinition `status.storedVersions` field after a failed migration, which allowed those versions to be removed from the CRD while objects were still stored in them.
143103.markdown: Fixed an issue where the storage version migrator removed old versions from a CustomResourceDefinition `status.storedVersions` field after a failed migration, which allowed those versions to be removed from the CRD while objects were still stored in them. ([#143103](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/143103), [@SEPURI-SAI-KRISHNA](https://github.com/SEPURI-SAI-KRISHNA)) [SIG API Machinery, Apps and Testing]
143103.author: SEPURI-SAI-KRISHNA
143103.pr_body:
#### What type of PR is this?

/kind bug
/sig api-machinery

#### What this PR does / why we need it:

When a StorageVersionMigration for a custom resource failed, the migration runner still trimmed the CRD's `status.storedVersions` down to the current storage version, just like after a success. A failed migration can leave objects in the old version ("N/M not yet migrated"). With the old version gone from `storedVersions`, it can be removed from the CRD. After that, those objects can't be decoded and LIST of the whole resource fails with `corrupt object ... request to convert CR from an invalid group/version`.

`finishCRDMigration` now updates `storedVersions` only when the migration succeeded, as KEP-4192 describes. A failed migration still sets the CRD's `StorageMigrating` condition to `MigrationFailed`.

#### Which issue(s) this PR is related to:

Fixes #143102

#### Special notes for your reviewer:

- The unit test case "Migration failed: CRD condition updated" expected `storedVersions: ["v2"]` after a failure. It now expects `storedVersions` to be left alone.
- `TestStorageVersionMigrationFailureKeepsStoredVersions` (integration) uses a ValidatingAdmissionPolicy to reject the migrator's patch of one CR, so the migration fails with that CR still stored as `v1`. It then checks that `v1` stays in `storedVersions` and that removing `v1` from the CRD is rejected. On master it fails with `Expected v1 to remain in status.storedVersions after a failed migration, got [v2]`; with this change it passes (ran it 3 times). The rest of `test/integration/storageversionmigrator` passes too.
- Clusters where a failed migration already trimmed `storedVersions` aren't repaired by this change.

#### Does this PR introduce a user-facing change?

```release-note
Fixed the storage version migrator removing old versions from a CustomResourceDefinition's status.storedVersions after a failed migration, which allowed those versions to be removed from the CRD while objects were still stored in them.
```

143111.text: Updated the PodDisruptionBudget controller to update PDB status when a Pod's labels change away from a previously matching PDB, and when multiple PDBs match the same Pod.
143111.markdown: Updated the PodDisruptionBudget controller to update PDB status when a Pod's labels change away from a previously matching PDB, and when multiple PDBs match the same Pod. ([#143111](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/143111), [@yankovitchg](https://github.com/yankovitchg))
143111.author: yankovitchg
143111.pr_body:
#### What type of PR is this?

/kind bug

#### What this PR does / why we need it:

The disruption controller only inspected the current pod on updates and only enqueued a single matching PodDisruptionBudget. That left PDB status stale when:

1. A pod's labels changed so it no longer matched a previously matching PDB (that PDB was never woken).
2. Multiple PDBs matched one pod (only one was enqueued, so the others' status could drift).

This change:
- Returns all matching PDBs from the helper and enqueues all of them from add/update/delete.
- On pod update, when labels change, also enqueues PDBs that matched the old labels (deduped with current matches).

Adds unit tests covering label-change enqueue of the previously matching PDB and enqueue of all overlapping PDBs on add.

/sig apps

Fixes #143043

143114.text: Fixed StatefulSet rolling updates counting unavailable Pods below `partition` against the `maxUnavailable` budget, which could stall the update, including when `maxUnavailable` is unset and defaults to 1. A percentage `maxUnavailable` is now calculated from the number of Pods in the update range (`replicas - partition`) instead of from all replicas.
143114.markdown: Fixed StatefulSet rolling updates counting unavailable Pods below `partition` against the `maxUnavailable` budget, which could stall the update, including when `maxUnavailable` is unset and defaults to 1. A percentage `maxUnavailable` is now calculated from the number of Pods in the update range (`replicas - partition`) instead of from all replicas. ([#143114](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/143114), [@yankovitchg](https://github.com/yankovitchg)) [SIG API Machinery and Apps]
143114.author: yankovitchg
143114.pr_body:
#### What type of PR is this?

/kind bug

#### What this PR does / why we need it:

With `MaxUnavailableStatefulSet` enabled, `updateStatefulSetAfterInvariantEstablished` counted unavailable pods across all ordinals when computing the rolling-update budget, but only deleted pods with ordinals >= `partition`.

An unavailable pod below the partition could fill the budget and stall the roll — including when `maxUnavailable` is unset (defaults to 1), which is supposed to stay behavior-neutral with the feature gate on. KEP-961 scopes `maxUnavailable` to pods staged by the partition.

This change counts unavailable pods for the **budget** only for ordinals >= `partition` (`updateMin`), matching the delete loops. The `UnavailableReplicas` metric continues to report unavailable replicas for the **whole StatefulSet** (not partition-scoped). Related unit tests are updated, including OrderedReady invariant cases and a metrics case with unavailable pods below the partition.

/sig apps

#### Which issue(s) this PR is related to:

Fixes #143042

#### Special notes for your reviewer:

- Budget / delete path: unavailable count for maxUnavailable uses ordinals >= `updateMin` (partition).
- `UnavailableReplicas` metric: still whole-StatefulSet (`unavailablePodsTotal`); intentionally not narrowed with the budget (per review).

#### Does this PR introduce a user-facing change?

```release-note
StatefulSet rolling updates with maxUnavailable no longer count unavailable pods below the partition against the update budget, which could previously stall Parallel rolls even when maxUnavailable was unset.
```

143147.text: Fixed an issue in `kubelet` where rotated container logs were deleted when writing their compressed copy failed (for example, on a full disk).
143147.markdown: Fixed an issue in `kubelet` where rotated container logs were deleted when writing their compressed copy failed (for example, on a full disk). ([#143147](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/143147), [@SEPURI-SAI-KRISHNA](https://github.com/SEPURI-SAI-KRISHNA))
143147.author: SEPURI-SAI-KRISHNA
143147.pr_body:
#### What type of PR is this?

/kind bug
/sig node
/area kubelet

#### What this PR does / why we need it:

`compressLog` ignored the errors from closing the gzip writer and the temporary file. Closing the gzip writer writes the rest of the compressed data and the trailer, so if that write failed (for example, the disk filled up), the kubelet still renamed the incomplete archive into place and deleted the original rotated log. The log was lost and the `.gz` was corrupt.

Both close errors are now checked. On failure, the temporary file is removed by the existing deferred cleanup and the original log is kept, so it gets compressed again on a later pass.

#### Which issue(s) this PR is related to:

Fixes #143146

#### Special notes for your reviewer:

`TestCompressLogKeepsLogWhenArchiveIsIncomplete` (Linux only) compresses an empty log with the temporary archive symlinked to `/dev/full`, so nothing is written during the copy and `Close` fails with `ENOSPC` when it writes the archive. It checks that `compressLog` returns an error, the original log is unchanged, and neither the archive nor the temporary file is left behind. The test fails on master (compressLog returns nil and removes the log) and passes with this change.

#### Does this PR introduce a user-facing change?

```release-note
kubelet: fixed rotated container logs being deleted when writing their compressed copy failed, for example on a full disk.

It controls whether manifest-based mutating webhooks run before webhooks registered through the API (`StaticFirst`, the default), after them (`StaticLast`), or sorted together with them by configuration name (`ByName`). 143160.markdown: Added the `staticOrder` field to `WebhookAdmissionConfiguration` for the `MutatingAdmissionWebhook` plugin (KEP-5793). It controls whether manifest-based mutating webhooks run before webhooks registered through the API (`StaticFirst`, the default), after them (`StaticLast`), or sorted together with them by configuration name (`ByName`). It requires `staticManifestsDir` and the `ManifestBasedAdmissionControlConfig` feature gate. Remove `staticOrder` before downgrading to v1.37 or earlier, because those versions reject it at startup. ([#143160](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/143160), [@aramase](https://github.com/aramase)) [SIG API Machinery, Auth and Testing]
143160.author: aramase
143160.pr_body:
#### What type of PR is this?

/kind feature
/kind api-change

#### What this PR does / why we need it:

Implements the mutating webhook merge order for KEP-5793.

Manifest-based mutating webhooks always run before webhooks registered through the API, so moving a webhook from a `MutatingWebhookConfiguration` to a manifest file changes the order webhooks run in. This adds a `staticOrder` field to `WebhookAdmissionConfiguration` for `MutatingAdmissionWebhook`:

- `StaticFirst` (default, same as unset): current behavior.
- `StaticLast`: manifest-based webhooks run after API-registered ones.
- `ByName`: both are stably sorted together by configuration name, like API-registered webhooks are today. A migrated `<name>.static.k8s.io` keeps its slot, except relative to configurations named `<name>-*`, or `<name>.*` that sort before `<name>.static.k8s.io` (for example `foo-bar` or `foo.bar.io`).

`staticOrder` requires `staticManifestsDir` and the `ManifestBasedAdmissionControlConfig` feature gate. `ValidatingAdmissionWebhook` rejects anything but `StaticFirst`. The merged list is cached, so there is no per-request cost. The effective order is logged at startup when `staticManifestsDir` is set.

#### Which issue(s) this PR is related to:

KEP: https://github.com/kubernetes/enhancements/issues/5793

#### Special notes for your reviewer:

- Design: kubernetes/enhancements#6417. Commits are API type, validation, merge behavior, integration test.
- `generic.NewCompositeWebhookSource` in `k8s.io/apiserver` is now unexported. Its only caller was in the same package, and its replacement takes the merge order.
- `--emulated-version=1.37` accepts `staticOrder` while a real 1.37 binary rejects it under strict decoding. Per the KEP it shares the existing beta gate, and since the field only lives in the local admission config file, a rollback fails at startup instead of silently changing the order.

#### Does this PR introduce a user-facing change?

```release-note
Add the `staticOrder` field to `WebhookAdmissionConfiguration` for the `MutatingAdmissionWebhook` plugin (KEP-5793). It controls whether manifest-based mutating webhooks run before (`StaticFirst`, the default), after (`StaticLast`), or interleaved by configuration name with (`ByName`) webhooks registered through the API. It requires `staticManifestsDir` and the `ManifestBasedAdmissionControlConfig` feature gate. Remove `staticOrder` before downgrading to v1.37 or earlier, which reject it at startup.
```

143221.text: ACTION REQUIRED: Changed `kubelet` to reject env-file entries with a hash immediately after a closing single quote, such as `KEY='value'#suffix`, instead of silently ignoring the suffix. Add a space or tab before an intended comment, or move an intended literal suffix inside the single quotes. Affected containers may fail to start until these entries are corrected.
143221.markdown: ACTION REQUIRED: Changed `kubelet` to reject env-file entries with a hash immediately after a closing single quote, such as `KEY='value'#suffix`, instead of silently ignoring the suffix. Add a space or tab before an intended comment, or move an intended literal suffix inside the single quotes. Affected containers may fail to start until these entries are corrected. ([#143221](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/143221), [@rishabhraj1572](https://github.com/rishabhraj1572))
143221.author: rishabhraj1572
143221.pr_body:
#### What type of PR is this?

/kind bug
/sig node

#### What this PR does / why we need it:

`ParseEnv` currently accepts `KEY='value'#suffix` and returns `value`, whereas Bash interprets that assignment as `value#suffix`.

The parser trims whitespace after the closing quote before checking for `#`, losing the distinction between a separated comment and an unquoted suffix.

This change rejects a hash immediately after the closing quote using the existing `unexpected content after closing quote` error. Comments separated by a space or tab remain supported, as do literal hashes inside quoted values.

Seven table-driven regression cases cover:
- Space/tab-separated comments after normal, empty, and multiline values.
- Adjacent hash suffixes after normal, empty, and multiline values.
- An invalid earlier entry when requesting a later key.

#### Which issue(s) this PR is related to:

N/A

Related precedent: https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/142665 addresses whitespace after `=`, rather than the closing-quote boundary.

#### Special notes for your reviewer:

This tightens accepted syntax. Previously accepted entries containing adjacent hash suffixes will now produce parsing errors and may prevent affected containers from starting or restarting.

For an intended comment, use:
`KEY='value' #suffix`

For an intended literal suffix, use:
`KEY='value#suffix'`

Maintainer feedback on this compatibility change is requested.

Validation performed during preparation on macOS/arm64 with Go 1.27.3:
- Four new rejection cases failed against the original parser.
- All seven new cases passed with the parser fix.
- `go test -count=1 -race -v ./pkg/kubelet/util/env` passed.
- `go vet ./pkg/kubelet/util/env` passed.
- Formatting and `git diff --check` passed.

Full kubelet, integration, end-to-end, Linux, and Windows tests were not run.

#### Does this PR introduce a user-facing change?

```release-note
Kubelet now rejects env-file entries with a hash immediately after a closing single quote, such as KEY='value'#suffix, instead of silently ignoring the suffix. Action required: add a space or tab before an intended comment, or move an intended literal suffix inside the single quotes. Affected containers may fail to start until these entries are corrected.
```

143223.text: Added the Alpha metric `kubelet_device_plugin_devices` in `kubelet`, a gauge of the number of devices the device manager knows about, broken down by `resource_name` and `health_state` (`healthy` or `unhealthy`). This makes devices reported unhealthy by a device plugin distinguishable from devices that are gone because the plugin deregistered, which previously both appeared only as a drop in allocatable.
143223.markdown: Added the Alpha metric `kubelet_device_plugin_devices` in `kubelet`, a gauge of the number of devices the device manager knows about, broken down by `resource_name` and `health_state` (`healthy` or `unhealthy`). This makes devices reported unhealthy by a device plugin distinguishable from devices that are gone because the plugin deregistered, which previously both appeared only as a drop in allocatable. ([#143223](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/143223), [@jianzhangbjz](https://github.com/jianzhangbjz)) [SIG Instrumentation and Node]
143223.author: jianzhangbjz
143223.pr_body:
#### What type of PR is this?

/kind feature

#### What this PR does / why we need it:

The device manager already tracks how many devices it considers healthy and unhealthy for each resource, and never reports it. The only device-plugin metrics kubelet exposes are `device_plugin_registration_total` and `device_plugin_alloc_duration_seconds`, so from outside a node the single observable symptom of devices going bad is `allocatable` shrinking — which conflates three different causes: the plugin reported devices unhealthy, the plugin deregistered, or the hardware is gone. An operator cannot tell them apart from metrics alone.

This adds `kubelet_device_plugin_devices{resource_name, health_state}`, an ALPHA gauge sourced from the sets `GetCapacity` already walks.

Two cases motivate it concretely. A healthy device turning unhealthy leaves node **capacity** unchanged, because capacity counts both sets and only allocatable counts healthy devices — so the event is at best inferable by diffing two other series. And a resource whose devices have all gone unhealthy looks exactly like a resource whose plugin went away, since both end up at zero allocatable.

#### Which issue(s) this PR is related to:

Related to #140656 (structured GPU device health reporting) and #123037 (observability of the kubelet managers). It does not resolve either: this reports only the healthy/unhealthy split kubelet already knows, and takes no position on the richer device-health API discussed in #140656.

#### Special notes for your reviewer:

**Why `GetCapacity`.** The counts change in four places, but `GetCapacity` is the one that already holds `m.mutex` and already iterates exactly `m.healthyDevices` and `m.unhealthyDevices` to compute capacity and allocatable, and its `deletedResources` loop is where resources are garbage collected. Instrumenting there is three lines in one function instead of four scattered sites, and the series cleanup falls out naturally. The refresh cadence becomes the node status sync rather than every `ListAndWatch` message, which seems right for a gauge.

**Why the series are deleted.** Resources really are removed from the maps in that loop, so without removing the series too, the last observed counts would be reported forever for a resource that no longer exists. The `GaugeVec` in `component-base` has no `DeletePartialMatch`, so this is two explicit `DeleteLabelValues` calls.

**Naming.** #140656 proposed `kubelet_device_health_state{resource,device,state}`. I went with `device_plugin_devices{resource_name,health_state}` to stay inside the existing `device_plugin_*` family and to follow `kubelet_running_containers{container_state}` — a gauge whose value is a count, with the state in a label. Happy to rename if reviewers prefer the other form.

**No per-device label, deliberately.** Whole-device plugins advertise one ID per card, where a `device` label would be fine. Shared-resource plugins advertise synthetic quota units instead — the RDMA shared device plugin publishes several dozen identical units per node — so a per-device label there yields many series that carry no information, because the IDs do not correspond to distinct hardware. Per-device detail is already available through the podresources API.

**Test.** `TestGetCapacityDevicePluginDevicesMetric` covers the initial split, a healthy-to-unhealthy transition that moves a device between the two series while capacity is unchanged, and removal of the series when the endpoint's grace period expires and the resource is garbage collected. I checked that it fails if the two label values are swapped and if the `DeleteLabelValues` calls are dropped, so it is not passing vacuously.

**Unrelated flake, for the record.** `TestDevicePluginReRegistrationProbeMode` fails intermittently for me on an unmodified tree — 3 of 5 runs on darwin/arm64, at `manager_test.go:291` expecting 1 and getting 2. It is pre-existing and not touched by this change, and I have not checked whether it reproduces on a platform CI actually runs.

#### Does this PR introduce a user-facing change?

```release-note
kubelet: added the ALPHA metric `kubelet_device_plugin_devices`, a gauge of the number of devices the device manager currently knows about, broken down by `resource_name` and `health_state` (`healthy` or `unhealthy`). This makes devices reported unhealthy by a device plugin distinguishable from devices that are gone because the plugin deregistered, which previously both appeared only as a drop in allocatable.
```

#### AI usage disclosure:

YES. The code and test in this PR were written with Claude Code, working from my analysis of where the counts were already tracked and unreported. I directed the design decisions above (instrumenting `GetCapacity`, the metric name, the absence of a per-device label), reviewed the diff, and ran the tests and the mutation checks described above. I am responsible for all of it; the usual disclaimer applies that no tool's output should be taken on trust, including mine.

143253.text: Fixed an issue where PodGroup and CompositePodGroup creation was rejected when `preemptionPolicy` was unset and the referenced PriorityClass specified `preemptionPolicy` as Never.
143253.markdown: Fixed an issue where PodGroup and CompositePodGroup creation was rejected when `preemptionPolicy` was unset and the referenced PriorityClass specified `preemptionPolicy` as Never. ([#143253](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/143253), [@alimaazamat](https://github.com/alimaazamat)) [SIG Scheduling and Testing]
143253.author: alimaazamat
143253.pr_body:
#### What type of PR is this?

/kind bug
/sig scheduling

#### What this PR does / why we need it:

Leave an unset `preemptionPolicy` in a PodGroup or CompositePodGroup unset until priority admission resolves it from the PriorityClass, matching the Pod admission flow.

Before, API defaulting set `PreemptLowerPriority` for PriorityClass before admission ran. A group referencing a different PriorityClass with `preemptionPolicy: Never` was then rejected even when the user omitted the group's policy.

Removed this early defaulting for PodGroup (`v1alpha3` and `v1beta1`) and for CompositePodGroup (`v1alpha3`). When policies are explicit it is kept, and priority admission continues rejecting policies that conflict with the PriorityClass. PriorityClass defaulting is unchanged when the policy is actually nil.

143261.text: Fixed a bug where pods with required pod affinity or anti-affinity terms using namespaceSelector were not requeued on assigned-pod events that could make them schedulable, which delayed scheduling until the periodic unschedulable-pods flush.
143261.markdown: Fixed a bug where pods with required pod affinity or anti-affinity terms using namespaceSelector were not requeued on assigned-pod events that could make them schedulable, which delayed scheduling until the periodic unschedulable-pods flush. ([#143261](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/143261), [@bolubo](https://github.com/bolubo))
143261.author: bolubo
143261.pr_body:
Supersedes #141954, which was closed accidentally during a force-push while applying review changes. This PR carries the same change plus the test cleanups requested in review there.

#### What type of PR is this?

/kind bug
/sig scheduling

#### What this PR does / why we need it:

A pod whose only scheduling blocker is a required podAffinity or podAntiAffinity term using namespaceSelector is not requeued when an assigned pod event could make it schedulable. The queueing hint was matching terms without resolving namespaceSelector, so the namespace side of the match never succeeded and the pod was only retried by the periodic unschedulable-pods sweep.

The hint now resolves namespace selectors without listing namespaces:

- It parses only the terms needed for the event: affinity for Pod ADD, anti-affinity for Pod DELETE, and both for Pod UPDATE.
- It fetches namespace labels with `nsLister.Get` only when a term can actually match the event pod.
- If the namespace is absent from the informer cache, it returns `Queue` conservatively instead of silently returning `QueueSkip`.
- If `Namespaces` already contains the event pod namespace, it skips the namespace lookup entirely.
- The Filter and Scoring paths keep their existing namespace-unrolling behavior; this change is limited to the assigned-pod queueing hint.

Namespace label updates are still outside this PR: waking pods on namespace label changes needs a Namespace cluster event resource, which the scheduler framework does not provide today. #141953 scopes that separately.

#### Which issue(s) this PR is related to:

Fixes #141953

#### Special notes for your reviewer:

- Scope: assigned-pod ADD/UPDATE affinity and anti-affinity, plus DELETE anti-affinity in both directions.
- Tests cover matching and non-matching event namespaces for ADD, UPDATE, and DELETE, including both DELETE directions.
- A table-driven lister test verifies that the hint never calls `List`, calls `Get` only when needed, and requeues conservatively on a namespace cache miss.
- A reverse-delete test uses an explicit namespace on the deleted pod so a wrong namespace lookup cannot pass accidentally via `NotFound`.
- Existing behavior for terms without namespaceSelector is unchanged.
- Verified with the interpodaffinity package tests, `-race`, the full scheduler plugins test set, `go vet`, and Go 1.27 gofmt.

#### Does this PR introduce a user-facing change?

```release-note
Fixed a bug where pods with required pod affinity or anti-affinity terms using namespaceSelector were not requeued on assigned-pod events that could make them schedulable, which delayed scheduling until the periodic unschedulable-pods flush.
```

This PR was written in part with the assistance of generative AI.

143267.author: SEPURI-SAI-KRISHNA
143267.pr_body:
#### What type of PR is this?

/kind bug
/sig auth

#### What this PR does / why we need it:

The truncate audit backend shallow-copied the event and then added `audit.k8s.io/truncated: "true"` to the copy's annotations. The copy shares that map with the original, so the original was marked too. The original is what the other audit backends receive and what later stages of the request reuse. With log truncation enabled and an audit webhook configured, the webhook got complete events, request bodies included, labelled as truncated.

`truncate()` now clones the annotations before adding the marker.

`TestTruncatingDoesNotModifyOriginalEvent` sends an oversized event through `audit.Union(truncate(fake), fake)` and checks that only the truncated copy carries the annotation, that the other backend keeps the request object, and that the original's annotations are unchanged. It fails on master and passes with this change.

```release-note
Fixed the audit truncate backend adding the audit.k8s.io/truncated annotation to events sent to other audit backends, which then reported complete events as truncated.

143278.text: Extended `workloadbuilder` validation to enforce hierarchy depth and size limits, parent-child scheduling policy and disruption mode compatibility, and uniform `priorityClassName` across the workload tree.
143278.markdown: Extended `workloadbuilder` validation to enforce hierarchy depth and size limits, parent-child scheduling policy and disruption mode compatibility, and uniform `priorityClassName` across the workload tree. ([#143278](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/143278), [@tosi3k](https://github.com/tosi3k))
143278.author: tosi3k
143278.pr_body:
#### What type of PR is this?
/kind feature

#### What this PR does / why we need it:
`kube-apiserver` and `kube-scheduler` restrict some workload configurations that `workloadbuilder` allowed so far. Adding matching restrictions to `workloadbuilder`'s own validation will make the library more robust and provide fail-fast mechanism for incorrect workloads.

Specifically, this PR extends workloadbuilder with the following checks:

- **Maximum tree depth (validateWorkloadItemTree)**: Rejects `WorkloadItem` hierarchies with depth exceeding `WorkloadMaxTreeDepth` (4, i.e. at most 3 composite levels and 1 leaf level).
- **Maximum children per composite node (validateWorkloadItemTree)**: Rejects any `WorkloadItem` with more than `WorkloadMaxPodGroupTemplates` (8) leaf children templates or more than `WorkloadMaxPodGroupTemplates` composite children templates.
- **Parent-child scheduling policy compatibility (Builder.Validate)**: Requires child groups to resolve to the `Gang` scheduling policy when their parent composite group uses `Gang`.
- **Parent-child disruption mode compatibility (Builder.Validate)**: Requires child groups to resolve to the `All` disruption mode when their parent composite group uses `All`.
- **Defaulted Basic scheduling policy handling (Builder.Validate)**: Treats an unset (nil or empty) `SchedulingPolicy` as `Basic` (matching compilation behavior) when validating `BuildOptions.AllowedPolicies`, `Basic` policy + `All` disruption mode incompatibility, and parent-child policy compatibility.
- **Uniform PriorityClassName across the hierarchy (Builder.Validate)**: Rejects trees where any item's resolved `PriorityClassName` differs from the root's, reporting a single error at the root path.

#### Which issue(s) this PR is related to:
N/A

#### Special notes for your reviewer:
/sig scheduling
/wg workload-aware-scheduling

#### Does this PR introduce a user-facing change?
```release-note
Extended workloadbuilder validation to enforce hierarchy depth/size limits, parent-child scheduling policy and disruption mode compatibility and uniform priorityClassName across the workload tree.
```

143286.markdown: Updated `kubectl apply` and `kubectl diff` to no longer fall back to fetching the deprecated `/openapi/v2` schema when calculating client-side patches. ([#143286](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/143286), [@seans3](https://github.com/seans3))
143286.author: seans3
143286.pr_body:
#### What type of PR is this?

/kind cleanup

#### What this PR does / why we need it:

Removes the deprecated `/openapi/v2` fallback (`OpenAPIGetter`) from `kubectl apply` and `kubectl diff` client-side patch calculation (`Patcher.patchSimple`).

OpenAPI v3 graduated to GA in v1.27. Previously, when applying or diffing a resource that does not use StrategicMergePatch (such as any Custom Resource / CRD), `gvkSupportsPatchOpenAPIV3` returned `false`, leaving `patch == nil` and unconditionally falling back to `p.OpenAPIGetter.OpenAPISchema()` (`GET /openapi/v2`) before computing a JSON Merge Patch. Removing this fallback avoids unnecessary `/openapi/v2` downloads on Custom Resource updates and keeps server-side lazy OpenAPI v2 construction (#140939) cold.

#### Which issue(s) this PR fixes:

Part of #126849

```

New ResourceClaim allocation results enforce equivalent validation for consumed capacity. Updates preserve unchanged capacity fields accepted under earlier validation. 143287.markdown: DRA ResourceClaim and ResourceClaimTemplate capacity requests now reject negative quantities, invalid capacity names, and maps containing more than 32 entries. New ResourceClaim allocation results enforce equivalent validation for consumed capacity. Updates preserve unchanged capacity fields accepted under earlier validation. ([#143287](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/143287), [@kvalliyurnatt](https://github.com/kvalliyurnatt)) [SIG API Machinery, Node, Scheduling and Testing]
143287.author: kvalliyurnatt
143287.pr_body:
#### What type of PR is this?
/kind bug
/kind api-change

#### What this PR does / why we need it:
The PR carry forwards the changes from #140563 

- For capacity requests in both exactly and firstAvailable, the API server now rejects negative quantities, invalid capacity names, and maps containing more than 32 entries. Equivalent checks apply to ConsumedCapacity when storing new ResourceClaim allocation results.
- Users receive immediate API validation errors for invalid capacity requests. Unchanged capacity fields that passed earlier, weaker validation remain accepted during updates, including metadata changes and finalizer removal.
- The scheduler also rejects negative consumed quantities and negative results after applying CapacityMultiplier when calculating DRA node-allocatable resource demand. These checks protect accounting when legacy or malformed allocation data is encountered.
- Map-size and quantity constraints use declarative validation; capacity-name validation remains handwritten. Generated validation, API documentation, and OpenAPI files are updated.

#### Which issue(s) this PR is related to:
Related to  https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/issues/140468

#### Special notes for your reviewer:
This is defense-in-depth. The scheduler should never receive negative capacity values after API validation, but it now explicitly rejects them if encountered.

```release-note
DRA ResourceClaim and ResourceClaimTemplate capacity requests now reject negative quantities, invalid capacity names, and maps containing more than 32 entries. New ResourceClaim allocation results enforce equivalent validation for consumed capacity. Updates preserve unchanged capacity fields accepted under earlier validation. The scheduler also rejects negative consumed quantities and computed footprints when calculating DRA node-allocatable resource demand.
```

143289.text: Added write-gating and leader recovery for leader election in `client-go`.
143289.markdown: Added write-gating and leader recovery for leader election in `client-go`. ([#143289](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/143289), [@michaelasp](https://github.com/michaelasp))
143289.author: michaelasp
143289.pr_body:
Implements the client-go part of KEP-6361 (Leader Election Recovery).

With LeaderElectionConfig.Recovery set, a missed RenewDeadline closes the write gate and calls OnStoppedLeading instead of ending Run. The elector keeps renewing the lease it held, never re-acquiring, and reopens the gate on success. Run returns if the lease changes hands or is deleted, when the recovery deadline passes, or on context cancellation.

LeaderElector.WriteGate returns a transport wrapper that rejects non-safe HTTP methods with ErrWriteGateClosed while not leading.

143290.text: Added `Pausable`, an optional client-go workqueue interface with `Pause` and `Resume` methods that controllers can use to stop and restart item retrieval; while paused, `Get` blocks, and `Add`, `Done` and `Forget` keep working.
143290.markdown: Added `Pausable`, an optional client-go workqueue interface with `Pause` and `Resume` methods that controllers can use to stop and restart item retrieval; while paused, `Get` blocks, and `Add`, `Done` and `Forget` keep working. ([#143290](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/143290), [@michaelasp](https://github.com/michaelasp))
143290.author: michaelasp
143290.pr_body:
Pausable is an optional interface, implemented by Typed and forwarded by the delaying and rate limiting wrappers. While paused, Get blocks until Resume or ShutDown; Add, Done and Forget keep working so event handlers can keep enqueuing and workers can finish the items they hold. A queue shut down while paused tells its workers to exit without handing out the remaining items.

This is the dequeue-blocking pause primitive from KEP-6361, used to stop controllers from reconciling while a controller manager's leader election write gate is closed.

143291.pr_body:
#### What type of PR is this?

/kind bug
/sig api-machinery
/sig network

#### What this PR does / why we need it:

Legacy Services and PersistentVolumeClaims lose their read-time defaults on cached watch events and status subresource requests, which can cause the ServiceCIDR repair controller to delete active IPAddress allocations after a status update. Combines #143279 with the regression tests from #143113 and #143228, moving read-time decoration into the storage decoder so defaults apply across reads, watches, and shared subresource stores, and status updates on legacy objects persist those defaulted fields to storage.

143340.text: kube-proxy no longer misses the initial Node zone when an already-running informer replays its cached Node, ensuring topology-aware routing uses the configured zone without requiring a restart.
143340.markdown: Kube-proxy no longer misses the initial Node zone when an already-running informer replays its cached Node, ensuring topology-aware routing uses the configured zone without requiring a restart. ([#143340](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/143340), [@zl86790](https://github.com/zl86790))
143340.author: zl86790
143340.pr_body:
#### What type of PR is this?

/kind bug

#### What this PR does / why we need it:

`NodeManager` starts and syncs the Node informer before kube-proxy creates its topology config. This means the informer is already running when `NewNodeTopologyConfig` adds its event handler.

Previously, kube-proxy set this up in two steps:

```go
nodeTopologyConfig := config.NewNodeTopologyConfig(...)
nodeTopologyConfig.RegisterEventHandler(s.Proxier)
```

Those two lines look sequential, but adding a handler to a running informer starts replaying cached objects on another goroutine. That goroutine can process the cached Node after the constructor installs the informer callback but before `RegisterEventHandler` runs.

When that happens, `NodeTopologyConfig` records the Node's zone with no downstream handler registered. A later update with the same zone is ignored because the topology labels have not changed, so the proxier can keep missing its zone until kube-proxy restarts. The informer callback can also read the handler slice while `RegisterEventHandler` writes to it.

This PR passes the proxier handler to the constructor. The handler is now stored before the callback is added to the informer, so cached Node replay cannot get between those two operations. Since `NodeTopologyConfig` only has one consumer, the handler slice and the separate registration method are removed as well.

A regression test starts and syncs the Node informer first, then creates `NodeTopologyConfig`, matching kube-proxy's startup order. It verifies that the cached zone is delivered to the handler. The config package also passes with the race detector enabled.

#### Which issue(s) this PR is related to:

Fixes #143275

#### Special notes for your reviewer:

Tested with:

```text
go test -race ./pkg/proxy/config
go test ./cmd/kube-proxy/app
```

#### Does this PR introduce a user-facing change?

```release-note
kube-proxy no longer misses the initial Node zone when an already-running informer replays its cached Node, ensuring topology-aware routing uses the configured zone without requiring a restart.
```

143356.text: Updated `kubeadm` to retry listing etcd members on transient errors during control plane join and reset, instead of failing on the first error.
143356.markdown: Updated `kubeadm` to retry listing etcd members on transient errors during control plane join and reset, instead of failing on the first error. ([#143356](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/143356), [@SEPURI-SAI-KRISHNA](https://github.com/SEPURI-SAI-KRISHNA))
143356.author: SEPURI-SAI-KRISHNA
143356.pr_body:
#### What type of PR is this?

/kind bug
/area kubeadm
/sig cluster-lifecycle

#### What this PR does / why we need it:

`Client.listMembers` was meant to retry `MemberList` until the `EtcdAPICall` timeout, but its poll condition returned the error, which makes `wait.PollUntilContextTimeout` stop right away. A single transient etcd error was enough to fail `GetMemberID` and `ListMembers`. During `kubeadm join --control-plane`, that left a freshly added learner unpromoted. `kubeadm reset` had the same problem during etcd member removal.

The condition now returns `false, nil` like the other etcd retry loops in this file. The last etcd error is still returned once the timeout expires.

#### Which issue(s) this PR is related to:

N/A

#### Special notes for your reviewer:

The retry is covered by a new `a transient error is retried` case in `TestListMembers`: the first `MemberList` call fails and the second succeeds. On master the poll aborts on the first error, so the case fails on both assertions, with `ListMembers() = []` and an unexpected error.

The new case needs a second `MemberList` attempt, and the table's shared 100ms deadline is shorter than the 500ms retry interval, so only one attempt ever happens under it. It therefore carries its own 3s `timeout` through a new per-case field; every other case keeps the 100ms default.

The failure counter lives in the test function rather than in the fake, because `listMembersOnce` calls `newEtcdClient` on every poll attempt and so gets a fresh `fakeEtcdClient` each time.

On the error returned after the deadline: once the condition stops returning errors, the only way `wait.PollUntilContextTimeout` fails here is the deadline, since the parent context is `context.Background()`. So the message states that and wraps the last etcd error as the cause, which keeps `errors.Is` working through it.

#### Does this PR introduce a user-facing change?

```release-note
kubeadm: retry listing etcd members on transient errors during control plane join and reset, instead of failing on the first error.
```

YES. An AI assistant helped find the bug and draft the fix and tests; I reviewed, ran and verified them.

143365.text: Fixed an issue where the Dynamic Resource Allocation (DRA) converting watch client did not terminate when stopped, which left its result channel open and kept draining the upstream watch.
143365.markdown: Fixed an issue where the Dynamic Resource Allocation (DRA) converting watch client did not terminate when stopped, which left its result channel open and kept draining the upstream watch. ([#143365](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/143365), [@alkaid040492](https://github.com/alkaid040492))
143365.author: alkaid040492
143365.pr_body:
#### What type of PR is this?

/kind bug

#### What this PR does / why we need it:

In `watchSomething.run`, the `<-w.stopChan` case of the `select` used a naked `break`, which only leaves the `select`, not the enclosing `for` loop. After `Stop()` the loop kept reading and converting events from the upstream watch and never reached the deferred `close(w.resultChan)` that `watch.Interface` consumers wait for. Changed to `return`.

Supersedes #141244 by @dwin-gharibi, who wrote the fix and the regression test. This PR applies the review feedback from that PR (drop the inline comment, reword the test comment, squash into one commit).

#### Which issue(s) this PR is related to:

Fixes #141243

#### Special notes for your reviewer:

In practice this is usually masked: `Stop()` calls `w.upstream.Stop()` first, and a well-behaved upstream closes its channel, which ends the loop through the `!ok` branch. The wrapper should still not depend on upstream behaviour for its own termination.

The new test uses an upstream whose channel stays open after `Stop()` and asserts that `run` returns and that queued upstream events are not drained. With the fix reverted it fails with `run did not return after Stop`.

#### Does this PR introduce a user-facing change?

```release-note
Fixed the DRA converting watch client not terminating when stopped, which left its result channel open and kept draining the upstream watch.
```

143378.text: Fixed a `kube-scheduler` panic when a ResourceSlice changed its device count while a matching DeviceTaintRule event was being processed.
143378.markdown: Fixed a `kube-scheduler` panic when a ResourceSlice changed its device count while a matching DeviceTaintRule event was being processed. ([#143378](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/143378), [@ahmadmaha02](https://github.com/ahmadmaha02))
143378.author: ahmadmaha02
143378.pr_body:
#### What type of PR is this?

/kind bug

#### What this PR does / why we need it:

A `DeviceTaintRule` event can reach `Tracker.syncSlice` after the ResourceSlice informer store has received an updated slice, but before the tracker has updated its cached copy. The two copies can then have different device lists.

For DeviceTaintRule events, `syncSlice` compares device taints by index to avoid a full deep comparison. If the updated slice has more devices than the cached one, that comparison reads past the end of the old list and panics.

This change checks the device counts first. If they differ, the tracker updates its cache and notifies listeners instead of comparing devices by index. The existing taint comparison remains in place when the counts match.

#### Which issue(s) this PR is related to:

N/A

#### Special notes for your reviewer:

`TestPatchChangedDeviceList` reproduces the event ordering deterministically: it updates the informer store from one device to three without running the ResourceSlice handler, then runs the DeviceTaintRule handler. Without the fix, the test panics at `tracker.go:551`. With the fix, it checks the patched slice and the update event sent to a listener.

Checks run locally from `staging/src/k8s.io/dynamic-resource-allocation`:

- `GOTOOLCHAIN=auto go test ./resourceslice/... -count=1 -timeout 300s` — passed
- `GOTOOLCHAIN=auto go vet ./resourceslice/tracker` — passed
- `git diff --check` — passed

#### Does this PR introduce a user-facing change?

```release-note
Fixed a kube-scheduler panic when a ResourceSlice changes its device count while a matching DeviceTaintRule event is processed.
```

143385.text: kubectl no longer treats arguments that contain `-v=` (for example the label `tier-v=8` or the selector `-l app-v=9`) as the log verbosity flag. Previously these silently raised the log level for the whole command.
143385.markdown: Kubectl no longer treats arguments that contain `-v=` (for example the label `tier-v=8` or the selector `-l app-v=9`) as the log verbosity flag. Previously these silently raised the log level for the whole command. ([#143385](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/143385), [@dhruv-techdev](https://github.com/dhruv-techdev))
143385.author: dhruv-techdev
143385.pr_body:
#### What type of PR is this?

/kind bug
/sig cli
/area kubectl

#### What this PR does / why we need it:

`GetLogVerbosity` (`staging/src/k8s.io/kubectl/pkg/cmd/cmd.go`) reads the klog verbosity from `os.Args` before cobra parses flags. It used `strings.Contains`, so any argument that merely contains `-v=` was treated as the verbosity flag:

```console
$ kubectl label pod foo tier-v=8      # sets verbosity to 8
$ kubectl get pods -l app-v=9         # sets verbosity to 9
```

`--v` is never actually passed, so cobra never resets the level, and the whole command runs at that verbosity. With a dummy kubeconfig, `kubectl label pod foo tier=8` prints 6 lines; `tier-v=8` prints 60, including request URLs and headers.

This PR switches the match to `strings.HasPrefix`, so only `-v=N` / `--v=N` are recognized, and adds a table-driven `TestGetLogVerbosity`. The function had no unit tests before.

#### Which issue(s) this PR is related to:

Fixes kubernetes/kubectl#1892 

#### Special notes for your reviewer:

- The fix is a one-line change in `cmd.go`. The rest of the diff is the new test in `cmd_test.go`.
- The new test fails on master for the three "value containing `-v=`" cases and passes with the fix. `go test ./pkg/cmd/` passes.
- The existing forms `--v=8`, `-v=8`, `--v 8`, `-v 8` and the `--` cutoff behave as before, and the test covers each of them.
- Introduced in kubernetes/kubernetes#131668 (v1.34.0).

#### Does this PR introduce a user-facing change?

```release-note
kubectl no longer treats arguments that contain `-v=` (for example the label `tier-v=8` or the selector `-l app-v=9`) as the log verbosity flag. Previously these silently raised the log level for the whole command.
```

#### What this PR does / why we need it:

##### Description
Bumps `cel-go` from `v0.29.2` to `v0.33.0`. The module moved to a new path, so it is now imported as `cel.dev/cel-go`. The CEL environment pins version options so that existing CEL expressions keep compiling and evaluating with essentially the same cost.
Changes include:
1. **Bump cel-go to v0.33.0 and update dependencies**
   - Replaces `github.com/google/cel-go v0.29.2` with `cel.dev/cel-go v0.33.0` in the root and staging `go.mod` files, and updates `vendor/` and `LICENSES/`.
   - Updates import paths to `cel.dev/cel-go/...`.
   - Updates `hack/unwanted-dependencies.json` for the new module path.
   - Links to cel-go in comments and API docs still point at `github.com/google/cel-go`, because many are pinned to old versions that only exist under the old path. As a result, the API types, OpenAPI specs and generated code are unchanged.
2. **Update CEL environment, cost estimation and tests**
   - **Environment pins** (`environment/base.go`):
     - `cel.CostModelVersion(0)` keeps the existing cost model. v0.33.0 defaults to a new one, which would shift CRD validation and admission policy cost budgets.
     - `cel.OptionalTypes(cel.OptionalTypesVersion(2))` keeps the current optional-types behavior instead of v0.33.0's newer default.
   - **Cost estimator** (`library/cost.go`):
     - `SizeEstimate` can no longer be converted directly to `CostEstimate`, so `.MultiplyByCostFactor(...)` is now called on the `SizeEstimate`.
     - Uses `cost.StringTraversalCostFactor` instead of the deprecated `common.StringTraversalCostFactor`.
   - **Tests:** updates expectations for the v0.33.0 behavior changes listed below.
3. **Replace deprecated cel-go cost aliases in CEL library cost estimator** (no behavior change)
   - In v0.33.0 the cost types and constants moved to `cel.dev/cel-go/common/cost`. The old names in `checker` and `common` are now deprecated aliases. This commit makes `cost.go` use the new names throughout (for example, `checker.CallEstimate` becomes `cost.CallEstimate`, `CostEstimate` becomes `cost.Estimate`, and `common.ListCreateBaseCost` becomes `cost.ListCreateBaseCost`).
   - Renames the parameter `overloadId` to `overloadID` (staticcheck ST1003).
   - The new names point to the same types and constant values, so behavior doesn't change. This clears the deprecation warnings from `verify-golangci-lint` and its PR-hints check.

#### Special notes for your reviewer:

##### What `CostModelVersion(0)` keeps, and what still changes
Pinning `cel.CostModelVersion(0)` keeps the cost formulas for each function from v0.29.2. Without the pin, v0.33.0 switches to its new cost model, which would change estimated and runtime costs for many functions.
Three changes are not controlled by the pin and still happen. Each was traced to the cel-go source and checked by running the same expressions on v0.29.2 and v0.33.0:
**1. Estimated cost of comparing `type()` values is now accurate instead of overflowing**
| Expression | Estimated cost before | Estimated cost after | Runtime cost (unchanged) |
|---|---|---|---|
| `type(self) == type(self)` | `1844674407370955268` | `5` | `5` |
| `type(self.nestedInMap['k1']) == type(self.nestedInMap['k2'])` | `1844674407370955272` | `9` | `9` |
- **Why:** the cost of `==` scales with the size of its operands. v0.29.2 had no fixed size for type values, so it treated the result of `type(x)` as unknown size (`MaxUint64`). The `==` estimate became `0.1 × MaxUint64`, about 1.8×10¹⁸. v0.33.0 treats types as fixed-size scalars (`isScalar` now includes `TypeKind`), so each operand has size 1. The `==` formula itself is unchanged.
- **Effect:** the estimate now matches the actual runtime cost. Only the estimate changes, not the runtime cost.

**2. Runtime cost no longer charges a call whose argument failed**
| Expression (measured with plain cel-go) | Runtime cost before | Runtime cost after |
|---|---|---|
| `"str1 " + ["a", "b", "c", "d"][4]` (index out of bounds) | 13 | 12 |
| `"str1 " + ["a", "b", "c", "d"][1]` (succeeds) | 13 | 13 |
- **Why:** in v0.33.0, a strict function call returns as soon as an argument evaluates to an error, without charging for the call. v0.29.2 charged the outer `+` even though its argument had already failed.
- **Effect:** only evaluations that end in an error change, and they cost slightly less. Successful evaluations cost the same. This is why `TestMessageExpression` expects a remaining budget of 48 instead of 47.

**3. Compilation error text changed**
- v0.33.0 adds ` (in container '...')` only when a container is set, so the usual message becomes `undeclared reference to 'foo'` instead of `undeclared reference to 'foo' (in container '')`.
- v0.33.0 can also add a "did you mean" suggestion when a declared name is close to the misspelled one.

143450.text: Fixed a regression in v1.37 where kube-scheduler could treat the devices of an allocated ResourceClaim as free after PreBind failed, which could lead to allocating the same device twice.
143450.markdown: Fixed a regression in v1.37 where kube-scheduler could treat the devices of an allocated ResourceClaim as free after PreBind failed, which could lead to allocating the same device twice. ([#143450](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/143450), [@troychiu](https://github.com/troychiu)) [SIG Node and Scheduling]
143450.author: troychiu
143450.pr_body:
#### What type of PR is this?

Optionally add one or more of the following kinds if applicable:
