#### What this PR does / why we need it:
When `PreBind` stores the allocation of a claim and then fails (e.g. binding conditions time out or another claim of the pod fails), `Unreserve` restores the claim in the assume cache to the informer copy. That copy usually still lacks the allocation, because the assume cache drops the informer event with the same ResourceVersion as the claim `PreBind` assumed. The devices then look free and pending pods get requeued for them, so the same device can get allocated twice. Claims reserved for a PodGroup aren't updated by `Unreserve`, so the PodGroup keeps failing with "got allocated elsewhere in the meantime".

Fix:
- `Unreserve` no longer restores the assume cache, for user claims and the extended resource claim.
- `PreBind` only assumes claims returned by the API server. When the status update of the extended resource claim failed, it used to assume the local copy with an allocation that was never stored.

143463.text: kube-scheduler: when the `GenericWorkload` feature gate is enabled, the scheduler logs an error at startup for each enabled PostFilter plugin that is not enabled at `PodGroupPostFilter` (for example, because it does not implement `PodGroupPostFilterPlugin`). Such plugins are not run for pods scheduled as part of a PodGroup.
143463.markdown: Kube-scheduler: when the `GenericWorkload` feature gate is enabled, the scheduler logs an error at startup for each enabled PostFilter plugin that is not enabled at `PodGroupPostFilter` (for example, because it does not implement `PodGroupPostFilterPlugin`). Such plugins are not run for pods scheduled as part of a PodGroup. ([#143463](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/143463), [@jdzikowski](https://github.com/jdzikowski)) [SIG Scheduling]
143463.author: jdzikowski
143463.pr_body:
#### What type of PR is this?

/kind feature
/sig scheduling
/wg workload-aware-scheduling

#### What this PR does / why we need it:

When the `GenericWorkload` feature gate is enabled, the scheduler framework now logs an error at initialization for each plugin enabled at the `PostFilter` extension point that is not also enabled at `PodGroupPostFilter`, e.g.:

```
"PostFilter plugin does not implement PodGroupPostFilterPlugin; it will not be run for PodGroups or CompositePodGroups" plugin="MyPostFilter" profile="default-scheduler"
"PostFilter plugin implements PodGroupPostFilterPlugin but is not enabled; it will not be run for PodGroups or CompositePodGroups" plugin="MyPostFilter" profile="default-scheduler"
```

Since #140412, PostFilter plugins are no longer run in a PodGroup scheduling cycle. Instead, the `PodGroupPostFilter` extension point (#139674) runs once when the whole PodGroup is unschedulable. A PostFilter plugin that does not implement `PodGroupPostFilterPlugin` (or is not enabled at `PodGroupPostFilter`) is therefore silently skipped for PodGroups. [KEP-5710: Pod Group Post Filter](https://github.com/kubernetes/enhancements/blob/master/keps/sig-scheduling/5710-workload-aware-preemption/README.md#pod-group-post-filter) asks for this safety check:

> For beta and GA we propose to disable all PostFilter plugins in the pod group scheduling cycle in favor of the newly added PodGroupPostFilter extension point. [...] We expect owners of out of tree PostFilters to follow with their own implementations.
>
> We will introduce additional safety check during the initialization, that will output an error log line when we detect plugins that implement PostFilter interface without implementing PodGroupPostFilter interface. This check will be only enabled when `GenericWorkload` feature gate is enabled.

This is also one of the KEP's [GA graduation criteria](https://github.com/kubernetes/enhancements/blob/master/keps/sig-scheduling/5710-workload-aware-preemption/README.md#ga): "Scheduler initialization check logging an error when `PostFilter` plugins do not implement `PodGroupPostFilter`."

#### Which issue(s) this PR is related to:

KEP: https://github.com/kubernetes/enhancements/issues/5710

#### Special notes for your reviewer:

- Only plugins enabled at the `PostFilter` extension point are checked (after `MultiPoint` expansion), not every plugin that implements the interface.
- The check verifies whether each enabled `PostFilter` plugin is present in `podGroupPostFilterPlugins`, logging distinct error messages depending on whether the plugin does not implement `PodGroupPostFilterPlugin` or implements it but is not enabled at `PodGroupPostFilter` (for example, configured only under `postFilter` or explicitly disabled under `podGroupPostFilter`).
- The default profile logs nothing: both in-tree `PostFilter` plugins (`DefaultPreemption`, `DynamicResources`) implement `PodGroupPostFilterPlugin` and are enabled via `MultiPoint`.

#### Does this PR introduce a user-facing change?

```release-note
kube-scheduler: when the `GenericWorkload` feature gate is enabled, the scheduler logs an error at startup for each enabled PostFilter plugin that is not enabled at `PodGroupPostFilter` (for example, because it does not implement `PodGroupPostFilterPlugin`). Such plugins are not run for pods scheduled as part of a PodGroup.
```

143495.text: Changed API validation to reject PodGroups, CompositePodGroups, and Workload templates that set the `all` disruption mode with a scheduling policy other than `gang` when they are created. Existing objects with this combination can still be updated.
143495.markdown: Changed API validation to reject PodGroups, CompositePodGroups, and Workload templates that set the `all` disruption mode with a scheduling policy other than `gang` when they are created. Existing objects with this combination can still be updated. ([#143495](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/143495), [@jdzikowski](https://github.com/jdzikowski)) [SIG Scheduling and Testing]
143495.author: jdzikowski
143495.pr_body:
#### What type of PR is this?

/kind feature
/sig scheduling
/wg workload-aware-scheduling

#### What this PR does / why we need it:

Disallows setting `disruptionMode.all` when `schedulingPolicy` is other than `gang` (`schedulingPolicy.gang == nil`) on newly created objects:
- `PodGroup` (`spec.disruptionMode`)
- `CompositePodGroup` (`spec.disruptionMode`)
- `Workload` (`spec.podGroupTemplates[*].disruptionMode`, `spec.compositePodGroupTemplates[**].disruptionMode`, and nested `podGroupTemplates[*].disruptionMode`)

With a non-`gang` scheduling policy (such as `basic`), pods are scheduled individually rather than as a gang, so a preemption disruption unit of `all` (which evicts the entire group together) would be larger than the scheduling unit. Checking `schedulingPolicy.gang == nil` rather than `schedulingPolicy.basic != nil` also ensures any future scheduling policy fails closed when paired with `all` disruption mode. This implements the [KEP-5710 GA graduation criterion](https://github.com/kubernetes/enhancements/blob/master/keps/sig-scheduling/5710-workload-aware-preemption/README.md#ga) requiring validation that the preemption unit is not bigger than the scheduling unit.

To preserve backwards compatibility for existing persisted objects on upgrade ([ratcheting validation](https://github.com/kubernetes/community/blob/main/contributors/devel/sig-architecture/api_changes.md#ratcheting-validation)), updates continue to allow existing non-`gang` + `all` configurations:
- `ValidateWorkloadUpdate` passes `WorkloadValidationOptions{AllowAllDisruptionModeWithNonGangPolicy: true}` to `ValidateWorkloadSpec`. Because `schedulingPolicy.basic`, `schedulingPolicy.gang` (`NoSet`/`NoUnset`), `disruptionMode`, and template lists (`NoAddItem`/`NoRemoveItem`) are immutable on update via declarative validation, an update cannot introduce a new non-`gang` + `all` template.
- `ValidatePodGroupUpdate` and `ValidateCompositePodGroupUpdate` only validate metadata updates (`spec.schedulingPolicy` and `spec.disruptionMode` are immutable), so existing `PodGroup`s and `CompositePodGroup`s remain updatable as well.

#### Which issue(s) this PR is related to:

KEP: https://github.com/kubernetes/enhancements/issues/5710

#### Special notes for your reviewer:

- Validation is implemented in `pkg/apis/scheduling/validation/validation.go` (matching #139596, as `validation-gen` declarative tags cannot express cross-field dependencies on union subfields) and verified in both imperative (`validation_test.go`) and declarative (`test/declarative_validation/scheduling/...`) validation suites.
- Existing scheduler integration tests that paired `BasicPolicy()` with `DisruptionModeAll()` have been updated to use `Gang` scheduling policy (`MinCount(1)` / `MinGroupCount(1)`), and unit tests in `pkg/scheduler/framework/preemption/` cover preempting pre-existing `Basic` + `All` victims.

#### Does this PR introduce a user-facing change?

```release-note
disallow setting "all" disruption mode on newly created PodGroups, CompositePodGroups, and Workload templates when scheduling policy is other than "gang" (existing objects remain updatable)
```

143534.markdown: With the alpha `WorkloadWithJob` feature gate enabled, the Job controller now finds the Workload and PodGroup for a Job by name. A Job that sets `spec.scheduling` gets its own Workload and PodGroup regardless of its owner, including Jobs created by a CronJob. A Job with a controller owner that does not set `spec.scheduling` gets none. A Job with the `scheduling.k8s.io/workload-name` or `scheduling.k8s.io/group-template-name` annotation selects a template in an existing Workload, and `spec.scheduling` is rejected when either annotation is set. ([#143534](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/143534), [@helayoty](https://github.com/helayoty)) [SIG API Machinery, Apps, Scheduling and Testing]
143534.author: helayoty
143534.pr_body:
#### What type of PR is this?

/kind feature

#### What this PR does / why we need it:
First of four PRs splitting #143128. 

This PR changes how the Job controller finds and manages the Workload and PodGroup for a Job when WorkloadWithJob is enabled:

- Discover the Workload and PodGroup by their deterministic names through the listers. The Workload/PodGroup informer indexes are removed.
- Pick the management mode from the Job object alone, with no lookups and no special case for the owner's kind. Rules are checked in this order:
    - spec.template.spec.schedulingGroup set -> the controller manages nothing.
    - scheduling.k8s.io/workload-name or scheduling.k8s.io/group-template-name set -> the controller manages the PodGroup only.
    - spec.scheduling set -> the controller manages both the Workload and the PodGroup, whatever the owner.
    - Otherwise, a Job with a controller ownerReference gets nothing, and a Job with no owner gets both with the Basic policy.
  Jobs created by a CronJob get a Workload and PodGroup only when jobTemplate.spec.scheduling is set.
- A Job with scheduling.k8s.io/workload-name or scheduling.k8s.io/group-template-name selects the template named by group-template-name in the external Workload named by workload-name.
- Include the Job UID in the PodGroup name, so sibling Jobs that select the same template get separate PodGroups.
- Copy `scheduling.k8s.io/parent-compositepodgroup` onto the PodGroup.
- Validate an existing root Workload to ensure it has exactly one `PodGroupTemplate`, and a `spec.controllerRef` that points at the Job. Also validate that an existing PodGroup references the expected Workload and template.
- Add the non-controller PodGroup ownerReference.
- Reject spec.scheduling when scheduling.k8s.io/workload-name or scheduling.k8s.io/group-template-name is set on a Job or on a CronJob jobTemplate.

If a scheduling object is missing or doesn't match, the sync returns an error and the Job is requeued, no pods are created. 

The follow-up PR replaces this with a `SchedulingBlocked` condition.

#### Which issue(s) this PR is related to:

KEP: https://github.com/kubernetes/enhancements/issues/5547

#### Special notes for your reviewer:
Stacked on [#143127](https://github.com/helayoty/kubernetes/issues/143127), which is stacked on [#142962](https://github.com/helayoty/kubernetes/issues/142962). Only the last commit is new in this PR.

#### Does this PR introduce a user-facing change?

```release-note
The Job controller finds the Workload and PodGroup for a Job by name. A Job that sets `spec.scheduling` gets its own Workload and PodGroup regardless of its owner, including Jobs created by a CronJob. A Job with a controller owner that does not set `spec.scheduling` gets none. 
A Job with the `scheduling.k8s.io/workload-name` or `scheduling.k8s.io/group-template-name` annotation selects a template in an existing Workload. `spec.scheduling` is rejected when either annotation is set.
```

"YES", helped with code and tests while I updated, tested, and reviewed the code and added more tests.

143557.text: kubeadm: fixed a bug where the error for missing CA files did not include the hint to run `kubeadm init phase certs ca`.
143557.markdown: Kubeadm: fixed a bug where the error for missing CA files did not include the hint to run `kubeadm init phase certs ca`. ([#143557](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/143557), [@devreddy1015](https://github.com/devreddy1015))
143557.author: devreddy1015
143557.pr_body:
#### What type of PR is this?

/kind bug
/kind regression
/sig cluster-lifecycle
/area kubeadm

#### What this PR does / why we need it:

When the CA files are missing, `getKubeConfigSpecs` is supposed to tell the user to run `kubeadm init phase certs ca` (added in #112941). Since #132080 switched kubeadm to its own errors package, that hint is never shown:

```go
if os.IsNotExist(errors.Unwrap(err)) {
```

`TryLoadCertAndKeyFromDisk` wraps the error twice, so a single `Unwrap` returns another wrapper, and `os.IsNotExist` does not walk wrapped errors. Before #132080 this was `errors.Cause(err)` from `github.com/pkg/errors`, which walked down to the `*fs.PathError`. Users now get the generic message:

```
couldn't create a kubeconfig; the CA files couldn't be loaded: failed to load certificate: couldn't load the certificate file /etc/kubernetes/pki/ca.crt: open /etc/kubernetes/pki/ca.crt: no such file or directory
```

This switches the check to `errors.Is(err, os.ErrNotExist)` and makes `TestGetKubeConfigSpecsFailsIfCADoesntExists` assert on the hint, so the test fails without the fix.

#### Which issue(s) this PR is related to:

N/A

#### Special notes for your reviewer:

This was the last remaining `errors.Unwrap` call in kubeadm outside `util/errors`.

#### Does this PR introduce a user-facing change?

```release-note
kubeadm: fixed a bug where the error about missing CA files is never returned.
```

YES. This PR was written in part with the assistance of generative AI (finding the bug, drafting the change and test). I reviewed and tested the change myself (`go test ./cmd/kubeadm/app/phases/kubeconfig/`).

#### What this PR does / why we need it:

When an `Info` has no REST mapping (for example with `--local`) and the kind is in a named API group, `Info.ObjectName()` returns `kind.group/name` with a trailing newline. error: poddisruptionbudget.policy/x

error: poddisruptionbudget.policy/x the object is not a pod or does not have a pod template: *v1.PodDisruptionBudget

`pdb.yaml` is any `policy/v1` PodDisruptionBudget. The "before" output is from a kubectl built from master. The "after" output is what the fixed message looks like; I haven't rebuilt kubectl to capture it.

143587.text: The `NodeSwap` feature gate, which graduated to GA and was locked to default in 1.34, has been removed.
143587.markdown: The `NodeSwap` feature gate, which graduated to GA and was locked to default in 1.34, has been removed. ([#143587](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/143587), [@antcybersec](https://github.com/antcybersec)) [SIG Node and Testing]
143587.author: antcybersec
143587.pr_body:
#### What type of PR is this?

/kind cleanup

#### What this PR does / why we need it:

Removes the GA `NodeSwap` feature gate.

The gate graduated to GA and was locked to default in 1.34. Under the three-release emulation window (`minRemovalVer = specVer.AddMinor(3)`), 1.38 is the first release where it can be dropped.

With the gate always on:

- kubelet config validation checks `memorySwap.swapBehavior` unconditionally. The error for setting it "when NodeSwap feature flag is disabled" is unreachable — a locked gate cannot be set to false — so it is removed.
- `GetContainerSwapBehavior` depends only on the swap controller being available.
- node status reports swap capacity whenever cadvisor reports it.
- in `kubelet_config_dir_test.go`, the block that preserved a job's `NodeSwap` override (for cgroupv1 CI images) has been dead since the gate was locked.

`NodeSwap` was the only user of the `featureGateDependencies` skip harness in `setters_test.go`, so that harness goes too.

The e2e feature label `feature.Swap` keeps the string "NodeSwap" — it is a ginkgo test selector, not a gate reference, and renaming it would reach into test-infra job configs.

Regenerated feature gate references via `hack/update-featuregates.sh`.

#### Which issue(s) this PR fixes:

Fixes #

#### Special notes for your reviewer:

One user-facing string changed: the cgroupv1 + LimitedSwap startup error said "swap feature is enabled and LimitedSwap but it is only supported with cgroupv2". It now reads "LimitedSwap is only supported with cgroupv2", since the old wording referred to a gate that no longer exists.

/sig node

#### Does this PR introduce a user-facing change?

```release-note
The `NodeSwap` feature gate, which graduated to GA and was locked to default in 1.34, has been removed.
```

143595.text: Fixed `kube-apiserver` sending an extra periodic bookmark to WatchList watchers about 1 second after the initial-events-end bookmark; these watchers now follow the regular bookmark interval.
143595.markdown: Fixed `kube-apiserver` sending an extra periodic bookmark to WatchList watchers about 1 second after the initial-events-end bookmark; these watchers now follow the regular bookmark interval. ([#143595](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/143595), [@serathius](https://github.com/serathius))
143595.author: serathius
143595.pr_body:
/kind bug

While adding tests validating exact Watch events, I noticed that cacher sends an extra bookmark 1s after the initial-events-end bookmark whenever new events have advanced the cacher's RV. This happens because WatchList watchers are registered in watcherBookmarkTimeBuckets with state cacheWatcherWaitingForBookmark, scheduling them for the first 1s bookmark sync instead of the regular 1m interval. 

This PR marks the bookmark as received in initWatcherIntervalLocked when initialEventsEndBookmark is present.

```release-note
WatchList will no longer send a periodic bookmark just 1s after sending initial bookmark
```

143604.text: kubeadm: `kubeadm upgrade diff` and the dry run of `kubeadm upgrade apply` and `kubeadm upgrade node` now include the etcd static Pod manifest when etcd is managed by kubeadm.
143604.markdown: Kubeadm: `kubeadm upgrade diff` and the dry run of `kubeadm upgrade apply` and `kubeadm upgrade node` now include the etcd static Pod manifest when etcd is managed by kubeadm. ([#143604](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/143604), [@asvw](https://github.com/asvw))
143604.author: asvw
143604.pr_body:
#### What type of PR is this?

/kind feature

#### What this PR does / why we need it:

Add the missing etcd manifest to `kubeadm upgrade diff` and to the dry run of `kubeadm upgrade apply` and `kubeadm upgrade node` when `etcd.local` is set.

An operator runs those previews to see what an upgrade will change. They show three of the four manifests the upgrade writes: kube-apiserver, kube-controller-manager and kube-scheduler. The etcd manifest is not shown, although the upgrade regenerates it from the ClusterConfiguration in the same way when etcd is managed by kubeadm. So a change to it shows only at `--v=4` during the upgrade itself ([staticpods.go#L232](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/f2a57ac2b9d3ea965421f0f72d1aa8b0dc6531e9/cmd/kubeadm/app/phases/upgrade/staticpods.go#L232)). A change to this manifest can move the etcd data directory. After a restore of etcd into a new directory with `etcd.local.dataDir` unchanged, `kubeadm upgrade diff` prints three image lines, and the upgrade then puts etcd back on the old directory (kubernetes/kubeadm#3335).

With the diff in both previews, they show what the upgrade will write for all four:

- `kubeadm upgrade diff` builds it with `GetEtcdPodSpec`, as the upgrade does, and diffs it against `/etc/kubernetes/manifests/etcd.yaml`. The file must exist, like the other three.
- The dry run calls `CreateLocalEtcdStaticPodManifestFile` with `isDryRun`, so the manifest is printed like the others. It runs before the other components, as in the upgrade, and only when `--etcd-upgrade` is not `false`. Patches apply as to the others.
- Both previews run `CheckEtcdDowngrade`, which checks the etcd version, before they build the etcd manifest. If the etcd on the node is newer than the version kubeadm would install, the upgrade and the previews skip etcd. `upgrade diff` logs a warning and leaves etcd out of the diff. The dry run prints the same message instead of the etcd manifest. If the check cannot read or compare the versions, the previews fail, as the upgrade does.

On a kind cluster of v1.37.0, etcd was restored into `/var/lib/etcd-restore` and `etcd.local.dataDir` still says `/var/lib/etcd`. There, `kubeadm upgrade diff v1.37.1` built from this branch prints:

```
[upgrade/diff] Reading configuration from the "kubeadm-config" ConfigMap in namespace "kube-system"...
[upgrade/diff] Use 'kubeadm init phase upload-config kubeadm --config your-config-file' to re-upload it.
--- /etc/kubernetes/manifests/kube-scheduler.yaml
+++ new manifest
@@ -19 +19 @@
-    image: registry.k8s.io/kube-scheduler:v1.37.0
+    image: registry.k8s.io/kube-scheduler:v1.37.1
--- /etc/kubernetes/manifests/etcd.yaml
+++ new manifest
@@ -34 +34 @@
-    image: registry.k8s.io/etcd:3.7.0-0
+    image: registry.k8s.io/etcd:3.7.1-0
@@ -91 +91 @@
-      path: /var/lib/etcd-restore
+      path: /var/lib/etcd
--- /etc/kubernetes/manifests/kube-apiserver.yaml
+++ new manifest
@@ -44 +44 @@
-    image: registry.k8s.io/kube-apiserver:v1.37.0
+    image: registry.k8s.io/kube-apiserver:v1.37.1
--- /etc/kubernetes/manifests/kube-controller-manager.yaml
+++ new manifest
@@ -32 +32 @@
-    image: registry.k8s.io/kube-controller-manager:v1.37.0
+    image: registry.k8s.io/kube-controller-manager:v1.37.1
```

Without this PR, the upgrade changes the `path:` line and nothing shows it beforehand. With it, the previews show it, as above. The image line comes from master's etcd version for 1.37.

#### Which issue(s) this PR is related to:

kubernetes/kubeadm#3335

#### Special notes for your reviewer:

`upgrade diff` applies no patches to the manifests it builds, the etcd manifest included. The upgrade skips etcd when the etcd on the node is newer than kubeadm's version for the target ([staticpods.go#L359](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/f2a57ac2b9d3ea965421f0f72d1aa8b0dc6531e9/cmd/kubeadm/app/phases/upgrade/staticpods.go#L359)). The check moved out of `performEtcdStaticPodUpgrade` into `CheckEtcdDowngrade`, and the upgrade calls it at the same point. The upgrade still fails when it cannot read or parse a version, and still skips etcd when the etcd on the node is newer. `CheckEtcdDowngrade` returns a bool that says which of the two it is, as `performEtcdStaticPodUpgrade` does, and the previews fail when the check fails, as the upgrade does. A dry run without a cluster, as after `kubeadm init --dry-run`, has no etcd manifest to read; the dry run then prints the etcd manifest as it prints the other three. The kinder dry-run job runs `kubeadm upgrade apply --dry-run` on such a node. A kind cluster of v1.37.0 runs etcd 3.7.0-0. To test, I set `etcd.local.imageTag: 3.6.8-0` in its kubeadm-config ConfigMap. `kubeadm upgrade diff v1.37.1` then logs `[diff] the desired etcd version "3.6.8-0" is older than the currently installed "3.7.0-0". Skipping etcd upgrade` and prints the other three hunks. The dry run prints the same line under `[dryrun]` and no etcd manifest.

Not in this PR: the `--v=4` level of the diff the upgrade itself logs (the same for all four components), and a warning when the data directory would change (what #143484 carried). Either can follow separately.

The `[dryrun] Would upgrade your static Pod-hosted control plane ...` line gets its missing trailing newline.

`TestRunDiff` gets four cases with local etcd. Three of them use an etcd manifest. One manifest is older and one is newer than the desired tag, and the test checks whether the etcd hunk is in the output. The third has `latest` as its tag, and the diff fails on it. `TestCheckEtcdDowngrade` runs the check on the same three manifests and on a missing one and checks the error and the bool of each. `DryRunStaticPodUpgrade` has no unit test and gets none here.

/sig cluster-lifecycle

#### Does this PR introduce a user-facing change?

```release-note
kubeadm: `kubeadm upgrade diff` and the dry run of `kubeadm upgrade apply` and `kubeadm upgrade node` now include the etcd static Pod manifest when etcd is managed by kubeadm.
```

#### AI usage disclosure:

YES. AI was used in the implementation and for drafting this description. I reviewed the change, ran the unit tests and tested it on my own kind cluster.

143628.pr_body:
#### What type of PR is this?

/kind bug
/sig cluster-lifecycle
/area kubeadm

#### What this PR does / why we need it:

`GetAvailableUpgrades` reads the cluster version from the kube-apiserver Pods (label selector `component=kube-apiserver,tier=control-plane`). If no Pod matches, `ComponentVersions` returns an empty map. `getLatestClusterVersion` then returns `(nil, nil)`, and `kubeadm upgrade plan` panics with a nil pointer dereference on `clusterVersion.LessThan(...)`.

This makes `getLatestClusterVersion` return an error when it finds no kube-apiserver Pods. `upgrade plan` then fails with a clear message instead of a panic. It also adds a unit test for `getLatestClusterVersion`. The empty-map case fails without the change.

#### What type of PR is this?

#### What this PR does / why we need it:

When the version to upgrade to is below `constants.MinimumControlPlaneVersion`, `EnforceVersionPolicies` returns:

143657.text: Updated github.com/go-jose/go-jose/v4 to v4.1.7 to address CVE-2026-116587 and five other advisories. JWK parsing now rejects RSA keys larger than 4096 bits, so an external OIDC issuer that uses a larger key will stop authenticating.
143657.markdown: Updated github.com/go-jose/go-jose/v4 to v4.1.7 to address CVE-2026-116587 and five other advisories. JWK parsing now rejects RSA keys larger than 4096 bits, so an external OIDC issuer that uses a larger key will stop authenticating. ([#143657](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/143657), [@H3xKatana](https://github.com/H3xKatana)) [SIG API Machinery, Architecture, Auth, Cloud Provider, Cluster Lifecycle and Node]
143657.author: H3xKatana
143657.pr_body:
#### What type of PR is this?

/kind dependency
/kind bug

#### What this PR does / why we need it:

Bumps `github.com/go-jose/go-jose/v4` from v4.1.5 to v4.1.7.

v4.1.5 is affected by CVE-2026-116587 (GHSA-mgcc-cww5-fp2q, high): a crafted
JWK with RSA parameters makes go-jose spend excessive CPU in
`rsa.PrivateKey.Validate`. Fixes for the advisory landed in v4.1.6.

v4.1.7 also ships fixes for five other issues listed in its release notes:
GHSA-r39w-98wm-9pp6, GHSA-27pc-rm86-68pq, GHSA-p9j4-2j95-j4rv,
GHSA-v6h2-qj3f-2h6v and GHSA-c67m-wr4h-2ccg. Those advisories were not yet
public when this PR was opened.

The library is used by kube-apiserver for service account token signing and
verification, by the external JWT plugin, by cluster-bootstrap, and by the
OIDC authenticator when it parses a JWKS from an external issuer.

Generated with:

```
hack/pin-dependency.sh github.com/go-jose/go-jose/v4 v4.1.7
hack/update-vendor.sh
```

#### Which issue(s) this PR is related to:

Fixes #143610

#### Special notes for your reviewer:

v4.1.6 introduces one behavior change: RSA moduli larger than 4096 bits are
rejected. This applies to JWK parsing, to RSA keys in `x5c` certificate
chains, and to RSA private keys. The limit is exposed as
`jose.MaxRSAModulusBits` and can be raised by a caller before parsing. An
external OIDC issuer that publishes RSA keys larger than 4096 bits will stop
authenticating against kube-apiserver. Keys of that size are rare, the failure
is closed rather than permissive, and no in-tree caller sets the variable
today. kube-apiserver's own service account keys are read as PEM or DER and do
not go through the JWK parser.

The diff is limited to `go.mod`, `go.sum`, staging `go.mod`/`go.sum` files,
`vendor/`, and `vendor/modules.txt`. No hand edits.

#### Does this PR introduce a user-facing change?

```release-note
Updated github.com/go-jose/go-jose/v4 to v4.1.7 to address CVE-2026-116587 and five other advisories. JWK parsing now rejects RSA keys larger than 4096 bits, so an external OIDC issuer that uses a larger key will stop authenticating.
```

143675.text: kubectl cluster-info dump now closes the files it writes with --output-directory, which avoids "too many open files" errors on large clusters.
143675.markdown: Kubectl cluster-info dump now closes the files it writes with --output-directory, which avoids "too many open files" errors on large clusters. ([#143675](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/143675), [@RoopanshuSD](https://github.com/RoopanshuSD))
143675.author: RoopanshuSD
143675.pr_body:
#### What type of PR is this?

/kind bug

/sig cli
/area kubectl

#### What this PR does / why we need it:

`kubectl cluster-info dump --output-directory=<dir>` opens one file per resource type per namespace, plus one log file per pod, through `setupOutputWriter`. None of those files were ever closed.

On a cluster with many pods or namespaces the process can hit its file descriptor limit (commonly 1024 on Linux) and abort with `too many open files`. On Windows the open handles also stop the output directory from being removed or moved until kubectl exits.

This PR:
- makes `setupOutputWriter` return a release function alongside the writer. The function is a no-op when output goes to stdout, because that writer is owned by the caller and must stay open.
- adds a small `printObj` helper that closes the file after each object is printed, replacing seven repeated call sites.
- closes the per-pod log file once all containers of that pod have been written.

#### Which issue(s) this PR is related to:

None. I found this while reading the `cluster-info dump` code.

#### Special notes for your reviewer:

Reproduction (before the change), Linux:

```
$ ulimit -n 64
$ kubectl cluster-info dump --all-namespaces --output-directory=/tmp/dump
```

On a cluster with more files to write than the limit, this fails with `too many open files`. <!-- TODO(author): run this against a real or kind cluster and paste the actual before/after output here. -->

Tests: `TestSetupOutputWriterFile` now asserts the file is closed after release, and `TestSetupOutputWriterNoOp` asserts the default writer is not closed. `go test ./pkg/cmd/clusterinfo/...`, `go vet` and `gofmt` are clean.

```release-note
kubectl cluster-info dump now closes the files it writes with --output-directory, which avoids "too many open files" errors on large clusters.
```

143695.author: jdzikowski
143695.pr_body:
#### What type of PR is this?

/kind bug
/sig scheduling
/wg workload-aware-scheduling

#### What this PR does / why we need it:

KEP-5710 requires all `PodGroupTemplates` and `CompositePodGroupTemplates` in a `Workload` to share one `preemptionPolicy` value, as they already share `priorityClassName` and `priority`. `validateWorkloadPriority` previously checked only `priorityClassName` and `priority`.

This change updates `validateWorkloadPriority` to also require matching `preemptionPolicy` values across all templates in the `Workload` hierarchy (treating unset and set as different values, consistent with `priority`). Updates skip the `preemptionPolicy` consistency check via `WorkloadValidationOptions` so `Workload` objects stored before this rule was added can still be updated.

143698.text: Fix `kubectl kuberc set --section aliases` to validate that alias names contain only alphabetical characters before writing to the kuberc file.
143698.markdown: Fix `kubectl kuberc set --section aliases` to validate that alias names contain only alphabetical characters before writing to the kuberc file. ([#143698](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/143698), [@muskan-creates352](https://github.com/muskan-creates352)) [SIG CLI]
143698.author: muskan-creates352
143698.pr_body:
#### What type of PR is this?

/kind bug

#### What this PR does / why we need it:

`kubectl kuberc set --section aliases` previously did not validate that `--name` contains only alphabetical characters (`^[a-zA-Z]+$`) before writing to the `kuberc` configuration file. Because `Preferences.Apply` validates alias names against `aliasNameRegex` during `kubectl` startup, setting an alias with non-alphabetical characters (such as `get-pods`, `get_pods`, or `get1`) succeeded and wrote an invalid `kuberc` file that caused every subsequent `kubectl` invocation to fail with exit code 1.

This PR exports `kuberc.ValidateAliasName` and calls it in `SetOptions.Validate()` when `--section=aliases`, ensuring invalid alias names are rejected before modifying or creating the `kuberc` file.

#### Which issue(s) this PR fixes:

Fixes kubernetes/kubectl#1896

#### Special notes for your reviewer:

/sig cli
/area kubectl

#### Does this PR introduce a user-facing change?

```release-note
Fix `kubectl kuberc set --section aliases` to validate that alias names contain only alphabetical characters before writing to the kuberc file.
```

143716.author: dom4ha
143716.pr_body:
#### What type of PR is this?

/kind bug
/sig scheduling

#### What this PR does / why we need it:
runPreEnqueuePluginsForPod observes scheduler_framework_extension_point_duration_seconds{extension_point="PreEnqueue"} in a deferred function that reads an outer s *fwk.Status. Both the gating-plugin branch and the plugin loop declared s :=, shadowing that variable, so the outer s stayed nil and the metric was always labeled status="Success", including when a PreEnqueue plugin gated the pod.

This assigns to the outer variable instead and adds a regression test covering the pass path, the plugin loop gating the pod, and the previously gating plugin gating it again. The test fails without the fix.

5. If the PR is unfinished, see how to mark it: https://git.k8s.io/community/contributors/guide/pull-requests.md#marking-unfinished-pull-requests

#### What type of PR is this?

/kind bug
/kind regression

#### What this PR does / why we need it:

When a Node is recreated with the same name while Kubelet is starting, early asynchronous CSINode initialization can read the dying predecessor Node and cache its UID in `nodeInfoManager.nodeID` for the lifetime of the Kubelet process. Subsequent CSINode creations then stamp that stale owner UID and are immediately deleted by the garbage collector.

This PR fetches the live Node UID directly in `CreateCSINode`, updates the cached `nodeID` when `tryUpdateNode` already fetches the Node during driver installation, and lazily re-fetches the live Node UID on ownership mismatch in `ensureNodeOwnsCSINode` before deleting an existing CSINode.

This fixes a regression introduced in 1.35 by PR #131098.

#### Which issue(s) this PR is related to:

Fixes #143719

#### Special notes for your reviewer:

**Testing performed:**
*   Ran `make test WHAT="./pkg/volume/csi/nodeinfomanager ./pkg/volume/csi" GOFLAGS="-v -race"` locally (all tests passed).
*   Manually verified on a live cluster running this build: had Kubelet cache a predecessor Node UID at startup, replaced the Node under the same name without restarting Kubelet, and confirmed Kubelet registered a CSINode with the new Node UID, survived garbage collection, and attached/mounted a CSI volume.

#### Does this PR introduce a user-facing change?

```release-note
Fixes an issue where kubelet fails to register CSINode objects when a node is quickly recreated with the same name, which previously prevented CSI volumes from attaching to the new node.
```

143784.text: Fix error reporting for invalid flags in kuberc aliases to display the alias name instead of the binary name.
143784.markdown: Fix error reporting for invalid flags in kuberc aliases to display the alias name instead of the binary name. ([#143784](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/143784), [@muskan-creates352](https://github.com/muskan-creates352))
143784.author: muskan-creates352
143784.pr_body:
#### What type of PR is this?

/kind bug

#### What this PR does / why we need it:

When an alias in the `kuberc` configuration is configured with an invalid flag or fails when applying a flag value, `Preferences.applyAliases` previously referenced `args[0]` (e.g. `kubectl`) in the error message instead of the alias name (`alias.Name`).

Because `args` starts with `os.Args[0]`, `args[0]` evaluates to the executable name, causing error messages like `invalid alias flag foo in alias kubectl`, which is confusing since `kubectl` is the root executable rather than the alias.

This PR updates `applyAliases` in `kuberc.go` to report `alias.Name` instead of `args[0]` on flag validation/application errors, and adds a test case in `kuberc_test.go` asserting the expected error format.

#### Which issue(s) this PR fixes:

Fixes kubernetes/kubectl#1900

#### Special notes for your reviewer:

/sig cli
/area kubectl

#### Does this PR introduce a user-facing change?

```release-note
Fix error reporting for invalid flags in kuberc aliases to display the alias name instead of the binary name.
```

143790.text: DeviceTaintEvictionController no longer counts a pod that is already terminating in `device_taint_eviction_controller_pod_deletions_total`, `device_taint_eviction_controller_pod_deletion_duration_seconds` or the `DeviceTaintRule` evicted pod count.
143790.markdown: DeviceTaintEvictionController no longer counts a pod that is already terminating in `device_taint_eviction_controller_pod_deletions_total`, `device_taint_eviction_controller_pod_deletion_duration_seconds` or the `DeviceTaintRule` evicted pod count. ([#143790](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/143790), [@imusmanmalik](https://github.com/imusmanmalik)) [SIG Apps and Scheduling]
143790.author: imusmanmalik
143790.pr_body:
#### What type of PR is this?

/kind bug
/sig scheduling
/wg device-management

#### What this PR does / why we need it:

`addConditionAndDeletePod` returns nil when the pod already has a `DeletionTimestamp`, and also after it deletes the pod. `maybeDeletePod` cannot tell the two apart, so a pod that someone else is already deleting gets counted in `device_taint_eviction_controller_pod_deletions_total`, in `device_taint_eviction_controller_pod_deletion_duration_seconds`, and in the `DeviceTaintRule` status as evicted, although the controller did not delete it.

`addConditionAndDeletePod` now also returns whether it deleted the pod, and `maybeDeletePod` skips the metrics and the rule count when it did not, the same way it already does for `NotFound`.

#### Which issue(s) this PR is related to:

Fixes #143789

#### Special notes for your reviewer:

`TestParallelPodDeletion` now has two cases. `deleted` is the existing scenario. `terminating` returns the pod with `DeletionTimestamp` set from the pod `Get` and expects no delete call, no event and no metrics. Without the fix it fails on the metrics:

```
-device_taint_eviction_controller_pod_deletion_duration_seconds_count 1
+device_taint_eviction_controller_pod_deletion_duration_seconds_count 0
-device_taint_eviction_controller_pod_deletions_total 1
+device_taint_eviction_controller_pod_deletions_total 0
```

Verified on linux/arm64 with golang:1.27: `go test -race ./pkg/controller/devicetainteviction/...`, the new test 20 times, `go vet`, `gofmt`, and `hack/verify-golangci-lint.sh` with both `hack/golangci.yaml` and `hack/golangci-hints.yaml`, all clean.

/cc @pohly

#### Does this PR introduce a user-facing change?

```release-note
DeviceTaintEvictionController no longer counts a pod that is already terminating in `device_taint_eviction_controller_pod_deletions_total`, `device_taint_eviction_controller_pod_deletion_duration_seconds` or the `DeviceTaintRule` evicted pod count.
```

143823.text: kubeadm: fixed a leak of one named pipe connection per responding CRI socket on Windows when detecting the container runtime socket.
143823.markdown: Kubeadm: fixed a leak of one named pipe connection per responding CRI socket on Windows when detecting the container runtime socket. ([#143823](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/143823), [@SEPURI-SAI-KRISHNA](https://github.com/SEPURI-SAI-KRISHNA))
143823.author: SEPURI-SAI-KRISHNA
143823.pr_body:
#### What type of PR is this?

/kind bug
/area kubeadm
/sig cluster-lifecycle

#### What this PR does / why we need it:

`isExistingSocket` decides whether a CRI socket exists by dialing it. The Windows implementation assigned the connection `winio.DialPipe` returned to `_` and returned `true`, so the connection was never closed. go-winio sets no finalizer on the handle, so nothing reclaimed it later either: every socket that answered the probe left a named pipe instance open until kubeadm exited. The unix implementation on the other side of the build tag does the same probe and closes its connection as soon as the dial succeeds.

`DetectCRISocket` goes through `detectCRISocketImpl(isExistingSocket, defaultKnownCRISockets)`, which probes containerd, CRI-O and cri-dockerd in turn, so one instance leaked per socket that answered, held against a live container runtime for the remainder of the command. `detectCRISocketImpl` returns an error when more than one socket answers, so the normal path leaked one.

kubeadm is short-lived and the handles go away with the process, so this is hygiene rather than a crash. It is still a resource acquired and never released, on the one platform where the sibling implementation releases it.

The Windows implementation now defers `Close` on the connection, after the error check so it only runs when the dial succeeded.

#### Which issue(s) this PR is related to:

N/A

#### Special notes for your reviewer:

- `winio.DialPipe` returns a nil connection together with its error, so the `defer` has to sit after the error check rather than straight after the call.
- With this change the close handling matches the unix sibling exactly: same `c, err :=` dial, same error check, same bare `defer c.Close()`. The two functions still differ in the pre-existing `npipe://` comment.
- The first revision also added a `runtime_windows_test.go`. It was dropped at review request, so the change is now just the `defer`.
- The package cross-builds and vets clean under `GOOS=windows`, and the existing `TestIsExistingSocket` still passes on linux.

#### Does this PR introduce a user-facing change?

```release-note
kubeadm: fixed a leak of one named pipe connection per responding CRI socket on Windows when detecting the container runtime socket.
```

#### AI usage disclosure:

YES. An AI assistant helped find the bug and draft the fix; I reviewed and verified it.
